title: BBQ Beef Sloppy Joe
description: Saucy barbecue beef piled on broiled buns, with romaine wedges in a dill and Dijon dressing on the side. Weeknight fast. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Ready in under 20 minutes. Contains egg, milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 850 kcal, 38g fat, 79g carbs, 39g protein. Stay by the oven while the buns broil; they go from golden to burnt quickly.
instructions: Chop half the pickles and all the dill (fronds and stems) finely. Cut the stem off the romaine, cut it in half across, then cut each half lengthwise into wedges that hold together. Slice the onion into thin rings.
Stir the Dijon, mayonnaise, dill and 4 teaspoons water together in a small bowl. Add salt and pepper to taste.

Set an oven rack at the top and turn on the broiler. Warm 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in big chunks until no pink remains, 3–4 minutes. Pour in all the barbecue sauce, let it bubble for 1–2 minutes, stirring now and then, and season with salt and pepper.
Butter the buns if you like and set them right on the top rack. Broil until just golden, 1–2 minutes.
Spoon the beef onto the buns and add a few onion rings. Dress the romaine wedges and scatter the chopped pickles over them.
Plate the sloppy joes with the salad, with the rest of the pickles on the side if you want them.

title: BBQ Meatloaf
description: Four small meatloaves under a sticky barbecue glaze, with roast broccoli and onion and a creamy sweet potato mash. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. If your broiler has a high setting, use it for the glaze. Contains egg, milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 760 kcal, 39g fat, 53g carbs, 38g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Put them in a large saucepan, cover by 1 inch with salted water, put the lid on and bring to a boil. Lower to medium and simmer uncovered until a fork goes in easily, about 8 minutes. Save ¾ cup of the cooking water, drain, return the potatoes to the pan and cover.
While they cook, chop 1 teaspoon garlic finely. Cut the onion in half and then into ½-inch wedges, keeping the core on so they hold. Break the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed.
In a medium bowl, mix the beef, chopped garlic, ½ cup panko, 2 large eggs, 2 teaspoons BBQ spice blend, 2 teaspoons salt and some pepper with your hands.

Toss the broccoli and onion with 2 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet. Form the meat into 4 ovals on a second sheet. Bake the meatloaves on the upper rack and the vegetables on the lower rack for about 15 minutes, until the meatloaves read 160°F inside and the vegetables are tender.

Take out the vegetables and cover them. Mix 2 tablespoons Worcestershire, ¼ cup ketchup and 2 teaspoons BBQ spice blend with a little salt and pepper. Turn the oven to broil, spoon the glaze over the meatloaves and broil on the upper rack until it browns in places, 2–3 minutes. Watch it closely.

Set the sweet potatoes back over medium heat. Add all the sour cream, the garlic herb butter and the saved cooking water, and mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Give the vegetables a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper, and serve everything together.

title: BBQ Pork & Grits Stuffed Peppers
description: Bell pepper halves filled with cheesy corn grits and barbecue pulled pork, baked under more cheese and finished with crispy onions. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 870 kcal, 49g fat, 76g carbs, 24g protein.
instructions: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and turn on the broiler. Cut the peppers in half lengthwise and pull out the stems and seeds. Lay them cut side down on a foil-lined rimmed sheet, rub with oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Broil the peppers on the middle rack until browned in spots and just tender but still firm, 5–7 minutes. Watch them. Turn them cut side up, switch off the broiler and set the oven to 400°F.

Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the scallions, keeping the dark green tops apart. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, soften the white and light green parts in 1 tablespoon butter for about 1 minute. Add the broth concentrate, 4 cups water and a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.

Whisk the grits into the boiling broth. Turn the heat to low and cook, stirring often so nothing sticks, until tender, about 7 minutes. Stir in the corn, half the cheese and 4 tablespoons butter. Season with salt and pepper.

Pat the pork dry and pull it into bite-size pieces. In a large bowl, toss it with the barbecue sauce, smoked paprika, half the crispy onions, half the dark scallion greens and 2 teaspoons vinegar. Season to taste. Spoon the grits into the peppers, pile the pork on top, and cover with the rest of the cheese.
Bake on the middle rack until the cheese is melted and spotted brown and a knife slides easily through the pepper, 15–20 minutes. Top with the remaining crispy onions and scallion greens to serve.

title: Bacon Skillet Meatloaf
description: One bacon-wrapped, barbecue-glazed meatloaf roasted in a skillet with broccoli around it, served with garlic mashed potatoes. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains egg, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 940 kcal, 48g fat, 65g carbs, 51g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the middle and upper third. Peel the potatoes if you like and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Cover by 1 inch with salted water in a medium saucepan, put the lid on and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover, turn to medium-high and cook until fork-tender, 10–12 minutes. Drain, return to the pan and cover.
Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Cut the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed, and toss them in a large bowl with 2 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper.

Gently mix the beef, panko, 1 tablespoon cowboy grilling rub and 2 large eggs in a medium bowl. Shape into a loaf about 8 inches long and set it in a large, heavy ovenproof skillet. Brush the top with 1 tablespoon barbecue sauce. Lay the bacon over it, overlapping a little if needed, and tuck the ends against the sides.

Roast the meatloaf on the upper rack for 10 minutes. Carefully add the broccoli around it and roast about 20 minutes more, until the center reads 160°F, the bacon is lightly browned and the broccoli has some color.

Meanwhile, warm the chopped garlic in 4 tablespoons butter in a small skillet over medium-high heat, stirring, until it sizzles and smells good, about 1 minute. Take it off the heat. Put the potatoes back over medium heat, add the garlic butter and ⅔ cup milk, and mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Move the broccoli to plates. Turn the oven to broil and broil the meatloaf on the middle rack until the bacon is crisp and deeply browned, about 5 minutes. Watch it. Brush the bacon with the rest of the barbecue sauce and broil 1–2 minutes more to caramelize it. Rest 5 minutes, then slice and serve with the potatoes and broccoli.

title: Baja Mahi Mahi Tacos
description: Crisp chipotle-battered mahi mahi in warm tortillas, with pico de gallo, shredded romaine and a lime-chipotle mayo. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: About 1 hour. Cod works just as well as mahi mahi. Contains egg, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 1020 kcal, 54g fat, 97g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes into ½-inch pieces. Seed the jalapeño if you like, then chop finely. Pull the cilantro leaves off; roughly chop half the leaves and slice the stems thin. Roughly chop ½ cup onion and keep the rest for another day. Cut the lime into 8 wedges. Halve the romaine lengthwise and shred it crosswise.

For the pico, mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, cilantro stems, chopped leaves, the juice of 4 lime wedges and a pinch of sugar. Season with salt and pepper. For the sauce, stir the mayo with ½–1 teaspoon chipotle powder and the juice of 2 lime wedges, thinning with water a teaspoon at a time until it drizzles. Season it too.

Whisk 1 cup flour with 1 teaspoon chipotle powder in a medium bowl, then whisk in 1 cup water until smooth. Add more water a tablespoon at a time until it is as thin as a loose pancake batter. Pat the fish completely dry, cut each fillet into 6 strips (24 in all), and season with salt and pepper. Spread ½ cup flour on a plate.

Heat a large heavy skillet, cast iron if you have it, over medium-high heat. Toast the tortillas in batches on one side until warm, about 30 seconds each, and stack them in foil or a clean towel. Then pour ¼ inch of oil into the same skillet and heat it over medium-high.

The oil is ready when a pinch of flour sizzles hard. Dredge half the fish in the flour and shake off the excess, dip in the batter, and lay it in the oil, carefully, as it may spatter. Fry, turning once, until golden and cooked through, 3–4 minutes. Drain on paper towels and salt right away. Repeat with the rest.
Fill the tortillas with fish, lettuce, pico and chipotle mayo, and scatter over the remaining cilantro leaves. Serve with the extra lime wedges.

title: Baked Chili Beef Taquitos
description: Spiced beef and melted cheese rolled tight in tortillas and oven-baked until crunchy, with quick pickled onions, enchilada sauce and guacamole for dipping. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 910 kcal, 43g fat, 76g carbs, 47g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Halve and thinly slice all the onions. Dice the tomatoes into ½-inch pieces. Oil a rimmed baking sheet.

Put a third of the sliced onions in a small bowl with 2 tablespoons vinegar, 2 tablespoons water, ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon sugar. Stir now and then while they pickle; you will use them at the end.

Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the rest of the onions with the tomatoes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden, 3–4 minutes. Add the beef, all the chorizo chili spice and a pinch of salt, and cook, breaking it up, until browned through, about 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in half the enchilada sauce and all the cheese, then season to taste. Lay the tortillas out and spread the filling along one edge of each in a strip about 4 inches by 1 inch.

Starting at the filled edge, roll each tortilla up snugly and set it seam side down on the sheet. Brush the tops and sides well with oil. Bake on the upper rack until crisp and golden, 15–20 minutes, checking toward the end.
Spoon the rest of the enchilada sauce over the taquitos and top with the pickled onions and cilantro. Serve the guacamole on the side.

title: Baked Rigatoni
description: A big pan of rigatoni layered with marinara, Alfredo and mozzarella and baked until bubbling, with a sharp Italian house salad of romaine, olives and pepperoncini. Makes a generous batch. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: About 1½ hours, including 20 minutes to cool before serving. Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 620 kcal, 26g fat, 70g carbs, 28g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle. Boil a large pot of salted water and cook the pasta, stirring now and then, just until it starts to soften but is still firm, 5–7 minutes. Drain and return it to the pot.
While the pasta cooks, tear or cut all the mozzarella into ½-inch pieces and grate the Parmesan if needed. Spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray.

Stir ¾ of the marinara, half the mozzarella and ⅓ of the Parmesan into the pasta, and season with salt and pepper. Spread a third of the pasta in the dish and cover it with half the Alfredo. Add another third of the pasta and the rest of the Alfredo, then the last of the pasta.

Spread the remaining marinara on top and scatter over the rest of the mozzarella and half the remaining Parmesan. Set the dish on a rimmed sheet, cover with foil and bake on the middle rack for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake until bubbling and browned, 25–30 minutes more. Let it cool for 20 minutes before serving.

Meanwhile, quarter the romaine lengthwise, cut it across into ¾-inch pieces and discard the root ends. Halve the tomatoes, slice the onion thin, cut the pepperoncini into rings (stems off), and halve the olives.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, onion, pepperoncini, olives and the last of the Parmesan in a large bowl and chill until dinner.
Shake the balsamic dressing with 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning in a small lidded jar and set aside.
Toss the salad with the dressing and season with salt and pepper. Serve with the rigatoni.

title: Barbacoa Beef Tacos
description: Shredded beef simmered with browned onion and Tex-Mex spice, piled into toasted tortillas with lettuce, radish, cilantro and a lime crema. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 660 kcal, 26g fat, 84g carbs, 29g protein.
instructions: Halve and thinly slice the onion, then chop 2 tablespoons of it finely for topping. Halve the lettuce lengthwise and shred it. Halve the radishes and slice them into thin half moons. Pull off the cilantro leaves and keep them for the end; slice the stems thin. Cut the lime into 8 wedges. Break the beef into bite-size pieces with your hands.

Warm 1 tablespoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Heat the tortillas one at a time until warm and lightly golden, about 30 seconds a side, and keep them wrapped in foil or a towel.
Add 1 tablespoon oil to the same skillet and cook the sliced onion over medium-high heat, stirring now and then, until soft with some browned edges, about 5 minutes.

Add the beef, Tex-Mex spice, cilantro stems and ½ cup water. Cook, stirring now and then, until the water cooks off, 2–3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat, add 3 tablespoons water and 1 teaspoon vinegar, and scrape up the browned bits. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, squeeze 3 lime wedges into a bowl and stir in all the sour cream and 1 tablespoon water, adding more water a teaspoon at a time until it drizzles. Season with salt and pepper.
Fill the tortillas with the beef and top with lettuce, radish and chopped onion. Drizzle with crema, add the cilantro leaves, and serve with the remaining lime wedges.

title: Barbecue Chicken & Pimento Cheese Grits
description: Barbecue-glazed chicken breasts over grits made creamy with cheddar, cream cheese and roasted red pepper, plus garlicky braised collards. A pimento cheese spread turned into dinner. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk. Per serving: about 590 kcal, 23g fat, 54g carbs, 49g protein.
instructions: Peel and finely chop 1 teaspoon garlic. Trim the collards, slice the stems thin crosswise and cut the leaves into bite-size pieces. Chop the roasted red peppers finely.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a medium Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and greens and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the broth concentrate and 1 cup water and bring to a simmer. Cover, turn to medium-low and cook until the greens are very soft, 12–15 minutes. Stir in 2 teaspoons vinegar, season with salt and pepper, and keep covered.

Bring 4 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Pour in the grits slowly while stirring. Turn the heat to low and cook, stirring now and then so they don't stick, until tender, about 7 minutes.
Stir the cream cheese, cheddar and chopped peppers into the grits. Season to taste, take off the heat and cover.

Pat the chicken dry, pound it to an even ½ inch if you like, and season with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken, 2–3 minutes a side. It won't be cooked through yet.

Spoon the barbecue sauce over the chicken and lower the heat to medium. Cook, turning, until the chicken is cooked through and glossy, 3–5 minutes. Lift the greens onto plates with a slotted spoon and add a splash of their liquid. Serve with the chicken and grits.

title: Beef Picadillo Pockets
description: Empanada-style pockets made easy with store-bought pizza dough, filled with beef, bell pepper, olives and golden raisins, and served with a bright cilantro-jalapeño chimichurri. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: About 1½ hours. Take the dough out at least 30 minutes ahead; at room temperature it relaxes and rolls out much more easily. Contains egg and wheat. Per serving: about 1190 kcal, 50g fat, 121g carbs, 52g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Take the dough out to warm up. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Roughly chop the olives, removing any pits. Seed the peppers and cut them into ½-inch pieces. Seed the jalapeños and chop them finely.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef, breaking it up, 5–7 minutes. Add the peppers and garlic and cook, stirring, until the peppers soften and color a little and the beef is cooked through, 5–7 minutes more.

Stir in all the cumin and oregano and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add 1 cup water and cook, stirring, until most of it has cooked off, 2–3 minutes. Move the mixture to a medium bowl, stir in the olives and raisins, season to taste, and let it cool for about 20 minutes.

Cut each ball of dough into 4 equal pieces, 8 in all. On a lightly floured counter, roll each into a 7-inch round. Spoon the filling onto the rounds, keeping a 1-inch border clear. Fold each over into a half moon and seal the edge by pinching or pressing with a fork.

Move the pockets to the lined sheet. Beat 1 large egg with 1 tablespoon water, brush it over the tops, and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Bake on the middle rack until puffed and golden, 18–22 minutes.

While they bake, roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Mix it in a small bowl with the jalapeños, ⅓ cup oil, 2 tablespoons vinegar and 2 teaspoons salt. Let the pockets cool for 5 minutes and serve with the chimichurri for dipping.

title: Black Bean Enchilada Casserole with Cheddar
description: All the flavor of cheesy enchiladas with none of the rolling: tortilla strips simmered straight into a spiced black bean sauce, then broiled under cheddar and scallions. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk. Per serving: about 550 kcal, 17g fat, 82g carbs, 23g protein.
instructions: Set a rack at the top of the oven and turn on the broiler. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Trim and thinly slice the scallions. Cut the tortillas into 1-inch strips. Drain and rinse all the black beans.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Add all but ¼ cup of the scallions and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic and all the taco seasoning and stir for 1 minute more.

Stir in all the tomato sauce, ¼ cup water, a pinch each of salt and sugar, and some pepper. Add the beans and tortilla strips and stir well. Simmer until thickened to a loose paste, 2–3 minutes, season to taste, and cover with the cheese.
Broil on the top rack until the cheese melts and the sauce bubbles, 2–3 minutes, watching closely. Rest 5 minutes, then scatter over the saved scallions and serve.

title: New York Strip Steak with Horseradish-Mint Glaze
description: Strip steaks with a peppery rub, seared hard and finished in the oven under a sweet, sharp glaze of mustard, honey, horseradish and mint. Easy enough for a weeknight, good enough for guests. Adapted from Bobby Flay via Matt Lee and Ted Lee, The New York Times.
notes: About 20 minutes.
instructions: Whisk the mustard, honey, horseradish and mint in a small bowl, season with salt and pepper, and set the glaze aside.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Mix the black pepper, red pepper flakes and salt in a small bowl and rub it onto one side of each steak.

Heat the oil in a medium ovenproof sauté pan over high heat until it smokes. Lay the steaks in rub side down and sear for 35 to 40 seconds, salting the top side as they cook. Turn them, move the pan to the oven and roast to medium rare, 8 to 10 minutes, brushing with glaze for the last 2 minutes. Brush with more glaze as they come out and rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Braised Beef Ragù with Gnocchi & Pesto Arugula Salad
description: Pan-crisped gnocchi tossed in a quick ragù of braised beef, marinara and Parmesan, with arugula dressed in basil pesto on the side. Adapted from Martha Stewart and Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 1020 kcal, 64g fat, 80g carbs, 34g protein.
instructions: Heat 4 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Separate any gnocchi stuck together and spread them in the pan in a single layer. Leave them alone until deep brown and crisp underneath, about 4 minutes, then stir and cook until just heated through, about 1 minute more. Move to a plate.

Grate all the Parmesan finely. Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef on both sides, 2–5 minutes total. Turn to medium, add ¼ cup water, and simmer while scraping up the browned bits.

Add the marinara, broth concentrate and ½ teaspoon granulated garlic and bring to a simmer. Stir in half the Parmesan. Turn to medium-low and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring now and then and breaking the meat into smaller pieces. Season to taste, add the gnocchi and toss to coat.
Toss the arugula with the pesto and 1 teaspoon vinegar in a large bowl. Serve the ragù topped with the rest of the Parmesan and some red pepper flakes, with the salad alongside.

title: Burst Tomato Burrata Pasta
description: Cherry tomatoes cooked low in garlicky oil until they burst into a sauce, tossed with pasta and fresh basil and topped with torn burrata. Adapted from How Sweet Eats.
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat and cook the garlic, dried basil and red pepper flakes for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and pepper and stir to coat. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes until the skins start to split. Turn the heat down if anything starts to scorch, or up a little if the tomatoes aren't bursting.
Meanwhile, boil the pasta in well-salted water.
Drain the pasta into the skillet and toss until every piece is coated. Turn off the heat, stir in the fresh basil, and add the burrata on top, torn into pieces or left whole.
Serve right away with Parmesan, more basil and a pinch of red pepper flakes.

title: Cacio e Pepe Crispy Chicken Sandwich
description: Crisp chicken cutlets on toasted buns under a peppery Parmesan and Alfredo sauce, with pepperoncini, paprika oven fries and a simple shallot salad. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains egg, milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 960 kcal, 42g fat, 113g carbs, 36g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into ¾-inch fries. Toss in a large bowl with 2 teaspoons paprika, 2 tablespoons flour, 4 teaspoons oil, salt and pepper. Spread them in one layer over 2 baking sheets and roast on both racks until browned and tender, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, halve the romaine lengthwise and slice it thin. Halve and thinly slice the shallot. Slice the pepperoncini. Grate all the Parmesan finely. Split the buns, then drizzle the cut sides and the chicken cutlets with oil and season with salt and pepper.

Turn the fries. Add the cutlets and the buns, cut side up, to the sheets and return them to both racks. Bake until the buns are toasted and the fries and chicken are cooked through, about 10 minutes. Keep an eye on them.
Meanwhile, whisk 2 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons vinegar and a pinch of sugar in a medium bowl and season. Toss in the romaine and shallot.

Whisk the Alfredo sauce, Parmesan, 2 tablespoons water and plenty of black pepper in a medium microwave-safe bowl. Microwave for 60–90 seconds in total, stirring every 30 seconds, until hot. Salt to taste.
Set the chicken on the buns, spoon on a generous amount of sauce, and add the pepperoncini. Serve with the salad, fries and any leftover sauce.

title: Carnitas Tostadas with Refried Black Beans
description: Oven-crisped corn tortillas spread with homemade refried black beans and topped with crispy chili pulled pork, melted cheese, pico de gallo and lime crema. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk. Per serving: about 890 kcal, 47g fat, 74g carbs, 31g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Halve the onion; slice one half thin and chop the other finely. Chop the tomatoes finely. Chop the cilantro stems finely and leave the leaves whole. Mix the tomatoes, cilantro stems, 1 tablespoon of the chopped onion and ¾ teaspoon each of vinegar and oil in a bowl, season, and set the pico aside.

Lay the tortillas on 2 rimmed baking sheets, oil both sides generously and sprinkle with salt. Bake on the upper and lower racks, swapping the sheets halfway, until crisp and spotted brown, 8–10 minutes in all. Watch them toward the end.

Meanwhile, melt 1½ tablespoons butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat and soften the rest of the chopped onion, 2–3 minutes. Add the beans with their liquid and cook, stirring, until the liquid has nearly gone, 7–9 minutes. Off the heat, mash the beans roughly, season to taste, and cover.

Break up the pork in a medium bowl and toss it with all the chili powder and ½ teaspoon sugar. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sliced onion until soft and browned, about 5 minutes, then move it to a plate. Spread the pork in the same skillet and leave it undisturbed until crisp in places, about 4 minutes.

Stir the onion back into the pork. Right on the baking sheets, spread the beans over the tortillas, add the pork, and sprinkle with the cheddar-jack. Bake on the middle rack until the cheese melts, about 4 minutes.

Grate the zest of half the lime into a small bowl and add 1 tablespoon lime juice, the sour cream and a pinch of sugar. Season, and thin with water if needed. Cut the rest of the lime into wedges. Top the tostadas with pico, crema and cilantro leaves, and serve with the lime wedges.

title: Cheesy Hasselback Potato Gratin
description: A gratin with the potato slices stood on their edges instead of laid flat, so the tops bake into crisp, cheesy ridges over a creamy middle. Adapted from NYT Cooking.
notes: About 2 hours, mostly three 30-minute bakes. Buy a potato or two extra: the slices need to be packed tight so they stay upright. A mandoline or food processor speeds up the slicing a lot. Let it rest a few minutes before serving.
instructions: Set a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 400°F. Mix the cheeses in a large bowl and put a third of it aside in another bowl for the top. Add the cream, garlic and thyme to the large bowl and season well with salt and pepper. Add the potato slices and toss with your hands, pulling apart any that stick so the cream gets between every slice.

Butter a 2-quart baking dish. Gather the slices into neat stacks and stand them on their edges in the dish, working from the outside in until it is full. Pack them very tightly; slice and coat another potato if there are gaps.
Pour the leftover cream mixture over the potatoes until it reaches about halfway up the dish. You may have some left.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake until the top is pale gold, about 30 minutes more. Scatter the reserved cheese over and bake until deep golden and crisp, about 30 minutes longer. Rest a few minutes, then serve.

title: Cheesy Skillet Gnocchi
description: Crisp-bottomed gnocchi in one skillet with roasted butternut squash, onion, rosemary and spinach, broiled under mozzarella and Parmesan. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 700 kcal, 23g fat, 103g carbs, 25g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Peel and thinly slice 2 large garlic cloves. Halve, peel and thinly slice the onion. Cut the squash into ½-inch pieces. Strip the leaves from three quarters of the rosemary and keep the rest for another use.

Toss the squash, onion, garlic and rosemary leaves with 3 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper in a large ovenproof skillet. Roast on the upper rack until the squash is tender with a few browned edges, 18–20 minutes. Tip into a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Shred the mozzarella on the large holes of a box grater and grate all the Parmesan finely if needed.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium heat. Separate any stuck gnocchi and add half of them in a single, slightly overlapping layer. Cover and cook without stirring until tender and golden and crisp underneath, 3–4 minutes. Move to a plate and repeat with the rest.

Take the skillet with the second batch off the heat. Stir in the spinach, the roasted vegetables and the first batch of gnocchi; the spinach will wilt in the heat. Add ⅔ cup water and season to taste.

Turn the oven to broil. Cover the gnocchi with the mozzarella and half the Parmesan and broil on the upper rack until melted and browned in spots, 1–3 minutes, watching closely. Serve with the remaining Parmesan at the table.

title: Chicken Al Pastor Quesadilla
description: Chicken and pineapple simmered in a tangy red enchilada sauce, folded into tortillas with cheese and baked until crisp, with a quick pineapple-cilantro salsa and crema. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Roll the lime firmly on the counter before cutting it and it will give more juice. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 630 kcal, 26g fat, 51g carbs, 47g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Halve and thinly slice all the onions, then chop 5 tablespoons of them finely. Roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Drain the pineapple, saving the juice, and chop the pieces roughly. Pat the chicken dry, cut it into 1-inch pieces if needed, and season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sliced onions until they start to soften, about 4 minutes. Add the chicken and cook, stirring now and then, until well browned, 5–7 minutes. Stir in the Tex-Mex spice and half the pineapple for 1 minute more, season, and move to a plate.

In the same skillet over medium-low heat, simmer the enchilada sauce, half the cilantro and the saved pineapple juice, stirring, until reduced by about half, 2–3 minutes. Stir in 1 teaspoon vinegar. Off the heat, stir in the chicken mixture and the cheese.

Oil a rimmed baking sheet lightly. Brush the tortillas with a little oil, lay them on the sheet, and spoon the filling onto them. Fold them into half moons. Bake on the middle rack, turning once, until the cheese is melted and the tortillas are spotted brown, 10–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the lime into 6 wedges. Mix the chopped onion, the rest of the pineapple and cilantro, and the juice of 2 lime wedges in a small bowl, and season. In another small bowl, whisk all the sour cream with 2 tablespoons water and season.
Serve the quesadillas with the salsa and crema.

title: Chicken Biryani
description: Chicken thighs and basmati rice toasted with ginger, garlic and curry powder, then baked with green beans and raisins, served with quick pickled onions, cashews and yogurt. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Contains milk and tree nuts. Per serving: about 770 kcal, 25g fat, 94g carbs, 46g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Slice the onions thin. Chop 2 tablespoons each of ginger and garlic finely. Trim the green beans and cut them in half. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. In a small bowl, toss ½ cup of the sliced onions with 2 tablespoons vinegar, 2 teaspoons sugar and ½ teaspoon salt, and leave them to pickle.

Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large Dutch oven or ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Soften the rest of the onions with a pinch of salt, 3–5 minutes. Add the chicken and brown it all over, 3–5 minutes. Stir in the rice, curry powder, ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant and the rice is lightly toasted, 1–2 minutes.

Stir in the green beans, raisins, 3 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt, and bring to a boil. Cover with an ovenproof lid or foil and bake on the middle rack until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through, about 30 minutes.
Roughly chop the cashews. Loosen the yogurt with 3–4 teaspoons water if you like, and season it.
Fluff the biryani with a fork and season to taste. Serve with the yogurt, pickled onions and cashews.

title: Chicken Chile Relleno
description: Roasted poblano halves stuffed with spiced ground chicken, quinoa and Monterey Jack, baked in a blender salsa ranchera made from the charred vegetables. Adapted from Plated.
notes: Read the whole recipe before starting. No blender? Chop the roasted garlic, onion, cilantro and jalapeño finely and stir them into the tomatoes. Cook ground chicken to 160°F. Vacuum-packed chicken can smell a little when opened; that is normal.
instructions: Heat the oven to 500°F. Bring the quinoa, 1 cup water and ¼ teaspoon salt to a boil in a small pot over high heat. Cover, lower to medium-low and simmer until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 15 minutes. Take off the heat and leave covered.

Meanwhile, rinse the produce. Drain the fire-roasted tomatoes, keeping the juice. Pick the cilantro leaves and discard the stems. Peel and halve the onion. Halve the poblanos lengthwise through the stem and scrape out the seeds. In a large baking dish, toss the whole garlic cloves, whole jalapeño, onion halves and poblanos with 1 tablespoon olive oil and ¼ teaspoon salt, and turn the poblanos cut side down.

Roast the vegetables until they start to char, 8–10 minutes. Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the spice mix, ¾ teaspoon salt and black pepper, then the chicken, and cook, breaking it up, until browned, 4–5 minutes. Take off the heat. Let the roasted vegetables cool for about 5 minutes.

Halve the roasted jalapeño and remove the seeds and stem. Put half of it in a blender or food processor (less or none for a milder sauce) with the drained tomatoes, roasted garlic, onion, half the cilantro and ¼ teaspoon salt. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Leave the poblanos in the dish and turn them cut side up.

Stir the quinoa, the saved tomato juice and half the Monterey Jack into the chicken. Fill the poblanos with it right in the dish, pour the salsa around them, and scatter any extra filling around the edges. Top with the rest of the cheese and bake until melted and starting to brown, 3–4 minutes.
Spoon the salsa onto plates, set the stuffed peppers on top, and finish with the remaining cilantro.

title: Chicken Curry with Rice
description: A 15-minute coconut curry of chicken and peas with browned onion, curry powder and chaat masala, spooned over quick-heated rice. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: About 15 minutes. No microwave? Put the rice in a skillet, sprinkle with water, cover and steam over medium heat until hot, 2–3 minutes. Contains coconut. Per serving: about 660 kcal, 27g fat, 66g carbs, 41g protein.
instructions: Halve and thinly slice the onion. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over high heat and cook the onion, stirring now and then, until soft and browned, 3–5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Stir in the curry powder, chaat masala and ¼ cup tomato paste for 1 minute. Add the coconut milk and all the broth concentrate and bring to a simmer. Simmer over medium heat, scraping the bottom of the pan, until a little thicker, 3–5 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked through, 2–4 minutes.
Stir in the peas and heat for 1 minute. Season to taste.
Heat the rice in the microwave following the package, or on the stove as in the notes, and serve the curry over it.

title: Chicken Cutlet Katsu & Cucumber Salad
description: Crisp chicken cutlets over sushi rice with sweet-tangy katsu sauce, a sesame-soy cucumber salad and quick gochugaru-pickled daikon. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains egg, milk, sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 850 kcal, 36g fat, 109g carbs, 25g protein.
instructions: Rinse the rice in a fine sieve until the water runs clear. Bring it to a boil with 2 cups water in a medium saucepan, then cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, 17–20 minutes. Keep the lid on until serving.
Meanwhile, cut the daikon into ¼-inch planks and then ¼-inch sticks. Halve the cucumbers lengthwise, scoop out the seeds if you like, and slice thin on an angle.
Whisk the tamari, sesame oil and 1 teaspoon rice wine vinegar in a medium bowl. Toss in the cucumbers and two thirds of the sesame seeds and season to taste.
In another medium bowl, stir 2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar with 2 teaspoons each of gochugaru, salt and sugar. Microwave 10–20 seconds until the sugar dissolves, then toss in the daikon.
Heat ¼ cup neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets until browned and hot through, 2–3 minutes a side, and drain on paper towels.
Fluff the rice into bowls. Top with the cucumber salad, pickled daikon and cutlets, drizzle the katsu sauce over the chicken, and sprinkle the remaining sesame seeds on the salad.

title: Chicken Milanese
description: Thin, crisp panko-crusted chicken cutlets with an arugula and cucumber salad in a lemon-dill vinaigrette and a creamy Dijon dip. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Pounding the chicken thin and even is what makes it cook fast and stay juicy. Contains egg, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 770 kcal, 49g fat, 38g carbs, 48g protein.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and put each breast between sheets of plastic wrap. Pound with a mallet or a heavy pan to an even ¼ inch. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Trim the cucumbers, peeling them if you like, and slice thin. Chop the dill, fronds and stems, finely. Squeeze 2 tablespoons lemon juice into a large bowl and cut the rest of the lemon into quarters.

Set up three bowls: 2 large eggs beaten with 1 tablespoon water and a pinch of salt and pepper; ½ cup flour with a little salt; and the panko. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, letting the extra drip off, then panko, pressing it on. Set them on a plate or tray.

Heat ⅛ inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of flour sizzles hard. Fry 2 cutlets at a time until golden, 2–3 minutes, then turn and cook until done, 1–2 minutes more. Drain on paper towels and season. Add more oil between batches if the pan looks dry.

Stir 1 teaspoon sugar into the lemon juice, then whisk in 2 tablespoons oil in a slow stream. Season and stir in 1 tablespoon of the dill. In a small bowl, whisk all the mayonnaise and Dijon with 1 tablespoon water and season.
Toss the arugula and cucumbers in the dressing and season. Scatter the remaining dill over the chicken and serve with the lemon wedges, salad, and the Dijon dip on the side.

title: Chicken Mole Poblano
description: Chicken breasts baked under a quick blender mole of cocoa, chipotle, peanut butter, raisins and tomatillo, with rice and a charred corn and tomatillo salad. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Contains peanuts. Per serving: about 960 kcal, 37g fat, 110g carbs, 54g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Bring the rice, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a medium saucepan, then cover and cook on low until tender, about 17 minutes. Leave covered off the heat. Meanwhile, chop the onion finely and chop 3 teaspoons garlic finely.

Husk the tomatillos, halve them and slice thin. Toss all but ⅓ cup with 2 teaspoons sugar and 1 teaspoon salt in a medium bowl and set aside for the salad. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large ovenproof skillet over high heat until it shimmers, add the corn, and cook, stirring now and then, until charred in spots, 3–4 minutes. Move to a plate.

Heat ¼ cup oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Cook half the onion, stirring often, until lightly browned, 4–6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook until it just starts to color, 1–2 minutes. Stir in 6 tablespoons cocoa powder for 15–30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the raisins, peanut butter, the remaining ⅓ cup tomatillos, ¼–½ teaspoon chipotle powder to taste, and 2½ cups water. Simmer over medium heat until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Blend until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry and season it. Put it in the skillet, pour the mole over, and bake on the middle rack until it reads 160°F inside, 10–15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes.

Chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Add the corn, the rest of the onion, half the cilantro, 2 tablespoons oil and 2 teaspoons vinegar to the tomatillos and season. Fluff the rice and serve with the chicken and mole and the salad, scattered with the remaining cilantro.

title: Chicken Piccata
description: Thin floured chicken breasts in a buttery lemon and caper pan sauce. Good with pasta, grains or plenty of vegetables. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk. Per serving: about 450 kcal, 27g fat, 12g carbs, 41g protein.
instructions: Chop 2 teaspoons garlic finely. Pick the parsley leaves, chop them finely and discard the stems. Zest the whole lemon and squeeze 2 tablespoons juice. Pat the chicken dry, pound it to an even ½ inch, and season with salt and pepper.

Spread ½ cup flour in a shallow dish and coat each piece of chicken, shaking off the extra. Heat ¼ cup oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it smokes. Cook the chicken, in batches if needed, until golden and cooked through, 2–3 minutes a side. Move to a plate and cover.

Add the garlic to the oil left in the pan and cook about 30 seconds. Add the capers, lemon zest and juice, and 1 cup water, and bring to a simmer over high heat, scraping up the browned bits. Let it reduce by half, 1–2 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in 4 tablespoons butter until creamy.
Season the sauce, stir in the parsley, and spoon it over the chicken.

title: Chicken Sausage Cacciatore with Gnocchi
description: A quick cacciatore-style ragù of chicken sausage, bell peppers and whole tomatoes, spooned over soft boiled gnocchi with Parmesan and parsley. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk (Parmesan) and wheat (gnocchi). Per serving: about 730 kcal, 17g fat, 98g carbs, 45g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Seed the peppers and cut them into thin strips. Snip the tomatoes in the can with kitchen shears until finely chopped.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the sausage and peppers, breaking up the sausage. Cover and cook, stirring now and then, until the sausage is lightly browned and cooked through and the peppers are tender, 5–8 minutes.

Stir in the garlic, ¼ cup tomato paste and 1½ teaspoons Italian seasoning for about 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, 1 cup water and a pinch of sugar and bring to a boil. Simmer over medium-high heat, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened, 5–6 minutes. Season to taste.
While it simmers, grate all the Parmesan if needed. Pick and roughly chop the parsley leaves. Separate any gnocchi that are stuck together.
Boil the gnocchi, stirring gently, until tender and most are floating, 2–3 minutes. Spoon into bowls, top with the ragù, and finish with parsley and Parmesan.

title: Chicken Sausage Minestrone with Farro & Spicy Sizzling Garlic
description: A hearty winter soup of chicken sausage, pinto beans, kale and farro in place of pasta, finished with a crackling garlic, rosemary and chili oil and toasted baguette. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: For no heat, leave the crushed red pepper out of the garlic oil. Contains soy and wheat. Per serving: about 840 kcal, 34g fat, 84g carbs, 44g protein.
instructions: Chop 2 cups onion finely. Chop 2 teaspoons garlic finely and keep 2 large cloves whole for the oil. Strip the kale from its stems and chop the leaves into bite-size pieces. Pick and roughly chop 2 tablespoons rosemary. Snip the tomatoes in the can with kitchen shears.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage, onion and chopped garlic, breaking up the meat, until the sausage is lightly browned and the onion soft, 5–7 minutes. Stir in half the rosemary for about 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring now and then, until the liquid has nearly cooked off, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the kale until just wilted, about 1 minute. Set an oven rack at the top and turn on the broiler.
Add the beans with their liquid, the farro and 6 cups water. Cover and bring to a boil, then set the lid ajar and cook over medium heat until the farro is tender, 18–20 minutes. Season to taste.

Meanwhile, slice the 2 whole garlic cloves paper thin. Put them in a small skillet with the rest of the rosemary, ½ cup oil and ¼–½ teaspoon crushed red pepper (or skip it). Cook over medium heat until sizzling and the garlic just starts to brown, about 3 minutes, then pour carefully into a heatproof bowl.

Split the baguette and broil it on the top rack until toasted, 1–2 minutes a side, watching closely. Drizzle the cut sides with olive oil and salt them. Ladle the soup into bowls, spoon over some of the garlic oil, and serve with the bread.

title: Chicken Shawarma Wraps
description: A 15-minute wrap: gyro-spiced chicken in warm pitas with tzatziki, cabbage, cornichons, olives and feta. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: About 15 minutes. Contains milk, sesame, soy, tree nuts and wheat. Per serving: about 590 kcal, 26g fat, 51g carbs, 40g protein.
instructions: Cut or pull the chicken into bite-size pieces, drizzle with a little oil, and season all over with the gyro spice.

Brush the pitas lightly with water on both sides. Warm them one at a time in a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat until soft and lightly browned, about 1 minute a side, and wrap in foil or a towel.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in the same skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken, stirring now and then, until browned and hot, 2–3 minutes.
Slice the cornichons thin. Fill the pitas with chicken, tzatziki, cabbage, cornichons, olives and crumbled feta.

title: Chicken Thigh Fajita Casserole
description: A one-skillet fajita dinner: taco-seasoned chicken thighs with peppers and onion under melted cheddar, topped with guacamole, fresh pico and lime. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk. Per serving: about 510 kcal, 32g fat, 18g carbs, 39g protein.
instructions: Set a rack at the top of the oven and turn on the broiler. Quarter the onion; chop one quarter finely and cut the rest into ½-inch pieces. Seed the peppers and cut them into ½-inch pieces. Mix all the taco seasoning with 1 teaspoon salt in a medium bowl, toss the chicken in it, and set aside.

Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Add the peppers and onion pieces, season, and cook, stirring, until the peppers soften, 5–6 minutes. Add a tablespoon of water at a time if the pan gets dry. Move to a bowl, cover, and keep the skillet.

Cut the tomatoes into ¼-inch pieces. Chop half the cilantro finely and keep the rest. Squeeze 2 teaspoons lime juice into a medium bowl and cut the rest of the lime into wedges. Add the tomatoes, chopped cilantro, chopped onion and 1 tablespoon oil to the juice, toss, and season.

Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and leave it until browned underneath, 2–3 minutes. Stir in ¼ cup water, carefully as it may spatter, scrape up the browned bits, and cook until the chicken is done, about 2 minutes.
Stir the peppers and onion back in and cover with the cheese. Broil on the top rack until melted, 1–2 minutes, watching closely.
Pick the remaining cilantro leaves. Top the skillet with guacamole, cilantro and some of the pico, and serve the rest of the pico and the lime wedges on the side.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: A one-tray bake: rice cooked right in a creamy tomato and garam masala sauce, topped with tandoori-spiced chicken, broiled, and finished with cilantro. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Contains milk (mascarpone). Per serving: about 730 kcal, 30g fat, 76g carbs, 45g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack at the top.

Whisk the tomato sauce, mascarpone, garam masala and 2 teaspoons each of salt and sugar in the tray. Stir in the rice and 1 cup water and cover with foil. Set the tray on a rimmed baking sheet and bake on the top rack until the rice is tender, 35–40 minutes. Take it out and turn the oven to broil.
Meanwhile, pat the chicken dry and toss it in a small bowl with the tandoori spice, 2 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper.
Fork the peas into the cooked rice and season to taste. Spread the chicken over the top in one layer and broil on the top rack until cooked through and browned in spots, 4–6 minutes.
Chop the cilantro, leaves and stems, and scatter it over before serving.

title: Chicken and Pesto Rice With Peas
description: Browned chicken thighs baked into a pot of rice cooked with broth and basil pesto, with peas stirred in at the end so the rice turns creamy. Adapted from Dan Pelosi.
notes: About 45 minutes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Season the chicken with about 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper and a pinch of crushed red pepper.

Heat the oil for a few minutes in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, stirring, until lightly browned but not cooked through, about 5 minutes, then lift it out.

Add the onion, garlic and about 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper to the pot. Cook over medium-low heat, scraping up the browned bits, until the garlic smells good, 2 to 3 minutes. Turn the heat to high, stir in the rice, broth and pesto, cover and bring to a boil, 3 to 5 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and stir the chicken and its juices into the rice. Cover and bake until the rice and chicken are cooked, about 20 minutes.
Stir in the peas, put the lid back on and let it sit 5 minutes so the peas cook and the rice gets creamy.
Serve with fresh basil, a squeeze of lemon and extra pesto.

title: Chili-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin
description: Pork tenderloin butterflied thin so it cooks in minutes, coated in chorizo chili spice and seared, with a charred corn and tomato salad and cool lime crema. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Cook the pork to 145°F inside. Contains milk (sour cream). Per serving: about 600 kcal, 40g fat, 22g carbs, 40g protein.
instructions: Slice each tenderloin through the side, parallel to the board, almost all the way through. Open it like a book and pound to an even ¼ inch. Mix 2 tablespoons oil with 2 teaspoons chorizo chili spice in a medium bowl, turn the pork in it, and leave it to marinate.

Zest the lime into a small bowl and stir in the sour cream, adding water a teaspoon at a time until spoonable. Season it. Squeeze the lime juice into a large bowl. Trim and thinly slice the scallions. Chop 2 teaspoons garlic finely.

Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in a large heavy skillet, cast iron if you have it, over medium-high heat. Add the corn, season, and leave it until browned in spots, 3–5 minutes. Move to a plate and wipe out the skillet.
Roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Halve the tomatoes. Stir the garlic and 4 tablespoons oil into the lime juice, then add the corn, cilantro, scallions and tomatoes. Season to taste.

Season the pork with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork, in batches if needed, until browned outside, just pink in the middle and 145°F inside, 3–4 minutes a side. Move to a board.
Spoon the crema over the pork and serve with the salad.

title: Chipotle-Shrimp Tacos
description: Grilled jumbo shrimp in a smoky chipotle, paprika and honey marinade, with creamy smashed pinto beans, a crunchy fennel and cilantro slaw, and sour cream. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: No grill? Use a grill pan on high. Contains milk, shellfish, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 720 kcal, 30g fat, 81g carbs, 40g protein.
instructions: Heat a grill to high if you're using one. Chop 4 large garlic cloves finely. Pat the shrimp dry. Whisk the tamari, honey, half the garlic, 2 tablespoons tomato paste, 1 tablespoon each of smoked paprika and vinegar, 1 teaspoon chipotle powder and 2 tablespoons oil in a bowl. Toss in the shrimp and set aside.
Drain and rinse the beans. Cut the lime into wedges. Halve the fennel, cut out the core, and slice thin. Chop the cilantro, leaves and stems, finely, and toss it with the fennel.

If you're using a grill pan, heat it on high now. In a medium skillet over medium heat, stir the rest of the garlic and smoked paprika with 1 tablespoon tomato paste, ½ teaspoon chipotle powder and 2 tablespoons oil until the paste darkens a little, 2–3 minutes.

Add the beans and ½ cup water and simmer, mashing about a quarter of them with a spoon, until creamy and most of the liquid is gone, 3–4 minutes. Off the heat, add lime juice and salt and pepper to taste. Cover.

Clean and oil the grill. Warm the tortillas until lightly browned, about 30 seconds a side, and wrap them as you go. Grill the shrimp until well charred underneath, 2–3 minutes, then turn and cook just until done, 30–60 seconds.
Dress the slaw with lime juice and oil to taste and season it. Build the tacos with beans, shrimp, slaw and sour cream, and serve with the lime wedges.

title: Chorizo-Black Bean Chili
description: A skillet chili of browned chorizo, black beans and red enchilada sauce, with homemade baked tortilla chips for scooping. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk (sour cream). Per serving: about 810 kcal, 24g fat, 95g carbs, 42g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Stack the tortillas and cut them into wedges. Oil two rimmed baking sheets, spread the wedges out in one layer, drizzle well with oil and salt them. Bake on both racks, swapping halfway, until crisp and golden, 20–25 minutes.

Pick the cilantro leaves and slice the stems thin. Halve and finely chop the onions. Halve the limes. Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large heavy skillet, cast iron if you have it, over high heat. Add the chorizo in big clumps, season, and leave it until well browned underneath, 3–5 minutes, then break it up.
Lower to medium-high. Add the cilantro stems and all but 4 tablespoons of the onion and cook, stirring often, until soft, about 4 minutes. Turn the heat down if it browns too fast.

Add all the enchilada sauce, the beans with their liquid, 2½ cups water, 1½ teaspoons salt and ¾ teaspoon sugar. Bring to a simmer over high heat, then lower to medium and cook, stirring now and then, until the chorizo is cooked through and the chili has thickened a little, 10–15 minutes.
Mash about a quarter of the chili with a potato masher or fork and stir to thicken it. Squeeze in the juice of half a lime and season to taste.
Top bowls with the saved onion, a spoonful of sour cream and cilantro leaves. Serve with the remaining lime and the chips.

title: Classic Patty Melt on Sourdough
description: The diner favorite: a thin beef patty with jammy onions and melted fontina, griddled in buttered sourdough, with a ranch wedge salad of tomato and cucumber. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: With a very large skillet or griddle you can cook more than 2 patties or sandwiches at once. Contains egg, milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 890 kcal, 49g fat, 52g carbs, 50g protein.
instructions: Quarter the lettuce lengthwise. Cut the tomatoes into bite-size pieces and slice the cucumber and onions thin. Shape the beef into 4 patties about ¼ inch wider than the bread and season both sides.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large heavy skillet over high heat until it smokes. Cook 2 patties until deeply browned and medium, 2–3 minutes a side, then repeat with the other two.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the onions and 2 tablespoons water, season, and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until the water is gone and the onions soften. Keep going, adding a splash of water whenever the bottom browns, until the onions are golden and jammy, 5–7 minutes. Stir in any juices from the resting beef.
Lay out the bread. Put half the cheese on 4 slices and half the onions over it. Add the patties, then the rest of the onions and cheese, and close with the remaining slices.

Melt 1 tablespoon butter in the skillet over medium heat until it foams. Cook 2 sandwiches, moving them now and then so they brown evenly, until golden and melty, 3–4 minutes a side. Repeat, keeping the finished ones on a sheet in a 200°F oven.
Arrange the lettuce on a platter, scatter over the cucumber and tomatoes, drizzle with ranch, and season. Halve the sandwiches and serve with the salad.

title: Coconut Curry Noodles With Shrimp
description: Noodles tossed in a quick South Indian-style coconut curry with ginger, garlic, warm spices and burst tomatoes, with shrimp cooked right in the sauce. Adapted from Zainab Shah.
notes: About 30 minutes. Tofu or vegetables work in place of the shrimp. Mustard seeds and curry leaves are optional but add depth and crunch.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.

Meanwhile, heat the oil on high in a 12-inch skillet or wok for 30 seconds. If you're using mustard seeds or curry leaves, add them and stir until the seeds pop and the leaves crisp, about 30 seconds.

Stir in the ginger, garlic, cumin, garam masala, crushed red pepper and black pepper, then the tomatoes and some salt. Cook, stirring now and then and lowering the heat if anything starts to catch, until the tomato skins soften, 3 to 5 minutes. Squash the tomatoes with a fork.
Pour in the coconut milk. When it boils, lower to medium and simmer 5 minutes. Add the shrimp and cook, turning once, until pink, 3 to 4 minutes. Turn off the heat.
Cook the noodles following the package, saving ¼ cup of the water before draining. Stir the noodles and the saved water into the curry and top with cilantro if you like.

title: Grilled Beef Tenderloin with Panzanella
description: Harissa-rubbed beef tenderloin off the grill with a bread salad of charred, garlic-rubbed ciabatta, marinated grape tomatoes, red onion and parsley. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: No grill? Broil the bread on the top rack until lightly charred, 1–3 minutes a side, and sear the beef in 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned and medium-rare, 3–4 minutes a side. Contains soy and wheat. Per serving: about 510 kcal, 28g fat, 30g carbs, 34g protein.
instructions: Heat a grill to high if you're using one. Halve the tomatoes lengthwise. Chop 1 teaspoon garlic finely and keep 1 large clove whole. Thinly slice ½ cup onion and save the rest. Pick the parsley leaves and set them aside; chop the stems finely.
Mix the tomatoes, parsley stems, chopped garlic, sliced onion, ¼ cup oil and 2 tablespoons vinegar in a large bowl. Season and leave to marinate.
If you're using a grill pan, heat it on high. Cut the ciabatta crosswise into 6 pieces, brush both sides with oil, and season.

Pat the beef dry, rub it with oil, and season all over with salt and 1 tablespoon harissa spice. Grill until well browned and medium-rare, 2–3 minutes a side, or longer if you prefer. Rest it on a board.
Grill the bread until lightly charred, 1–3 minutes a side, watching it. Rub with the whole garlic clove and tear into 2-inch pieces.
Toss the bread and parsley leaves into the tomatoes and season. Slice the beef if you like and serve with the salad.

title: Cottage Pie
description: Ground beef in a thick red wine gravy with carrot, celery, onion and peas, covered in Parmesan mashed potatoes and baked until golden. Cheap, filling and freezes well. Adapted from Dan Pelosi.
notes: About 2 hours. No ovenproof skillet? Build it in a 9x13-inch baking dish instead. Other vegetables work in the base, and sweet potatoes work on top.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F.

Warm an ovenproof 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook the beef with a big pinch of salt, breaking it up, until just cooked with a little pink left, 5 to 7 minutes. Lift it into a bowl with a slotted spoon. Pour off all but about a teaspoon of the fat.

Add the butter, onion, celery, carrot and a pinch of salt to the skillet. Cook, stirring now and then, until the onion is translucent and the carrot just tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for about 1 minute, then stir in the flour.

Add the broth, red wine, peas, Worcestershire, thyme sprigs, bay leaves and 1 teaspoon each of salt and pepper. Simmer, stirring now and then, until it is as thick as gravy, 7 to 10 minutes. Taste for seasoning, pull out the bay leaves and thyme, and stir the beef back in. Let it cool a little off the heat.

Bring 4 quarts water and 2 tablespoons salt to a boil in a large saucepan. Cook the potatoes until a knife slides in easily, about 15 minutes. Drain, return them to the pan, and add the milk, 4 tablespoons butter and ½ cup Parmesan. Mash just until creamy; don't overwork them. Salt to taste.

Spoon the potatoes over the filling and spread them right to the edges. Drizzle with the last tablespoon of butter, sprinkle with the remaining ¼ cup Parmesan, and bake until golden and bubbling, about 30 minutes. Let it stand 10 minutes before serving.

title: Creamy Chicken & Gnocchi Dumplings with Pot Pie Gravy
description: Chicken pot pie flavors in a skillet: chicken, carrots and peas in a creamy gravy, with soft gnocchi standing in for dumplings. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 630 kcal, 13g fat, 86g carbs, 47g protein.
instructions: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to a boil. Cook the gnocchi, stirring gently, until tender and most are floating, about 3 minutes. Drain well and set aside.
Meanwhile, scrub and trim half the carrots (save the rest), halve them lengthwise and slice into ¼-inch half moons. Trim and thinly slice the scallions.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the carrots, scallions and a sprig of thyme, season, and cook, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly browned, 3–4 minutes.

Pat the chicken dry and add it to the skillet with a pinch of salt and pepper. Leave it until browned underneath and cooked through, about 3 minutes. Stir in 2 tablespoons flour and cook about 1 minute more.
Pour in all the broth concentrate and 2 cups milk and bring to a simmer. Stir in the peas and gnocchi and cook over medium heat until the peas are tender, 3–4 minutes. Season to taste.
Take out the thyme sprig. Loosen the sauce with water, a tablespoon at a time, until it is how you like it, and scatter torn parsley over the top.

title: Creamy Chorizo Carbonara
description: Carbonara made with crisp, smoky chorizo instead of guanciale, a lemony egg and Parmesan sauce, and crispy onions on top, with lemon green beans on the side. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: To separate an egg, crack it into a small bowl and lift the yolk out with a spoon or half the shell. Keep the whites for an omelet. Contains egg, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 630 kcal, 16g fat, 76g carbs, 44g protein.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil. Grate all the Parmesan finely. Zest half the lemon and cut the rest into wedges. Whisk the zest, three quarters of the Parmesan, 1 tablespoon vinegar, 2 whole eggs and 2 egg yolks in a medium bowl.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook all the chorizo, breaking it up small, until deeply browned and the fat has run out, 8–10 minutes. Pour the fat into a small bowl. Turn the heat to medium, add 3 tablespoons water and scrape up the browned bits, then lower to medium-low.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta, stirring now and then, until al dente, 8–10 minutes. Save 1 cup of the water and drain. Toss the pasta into the skillet with 2 tablespoons of the chorizo fat.

Whisk ½ cup of the pasta water slowly into the egg mixture; it will look thin. With the pasta over medium-low heat, pour in the egg mixture while stirring, and keep stirring until the sauce thickens and clings, 1–3 minutes. Loosen with more pasta water a tablespoon at a time if needed.
Put the green beans in a large microwave-safe bowl, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave until tender, 3–5 minutes. Season and squeeze over some lemon.
Roughly chop the parsley leaves. Plate the pasta and top with parsley, the rest of the Parmesan, crispy onions and a drizzle of the chorizo fat. Serve the beans alongside.

title: Creamy Miso Pork Ramen
description: A rich, thick ramen of ground pork and chewy noodles in a broth made silky with miso, hondashi, eggs and mayonnaise. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: For a soupier bowl, add a cup or two of chicken or vegetable stock. More toppings are welcome: a soft egg, spinach, chard or corn. Contains egg, fish, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 660 kcal, 31g fat, 62g carbs, 38g protein.
instructions: Grate 3 large garlic cloves into a large bowl and whisk in the mayonnaise, ramen base, hondashi, miso and 4 large eggs until smooth. Trim and thinly slice the scallions, keeping the dark greens apart.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and stir the scallion whites and light greens until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the pork and break it up until no pink remains, 2–3 minutes. Add 9 cups water and bring to a boil, then add the noodles. Cook, stirring so they don't clump, until the noodles are al dente and the pork is cooked through, 4–5 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat. Whisk 1 cup of the hot broth into the egg mixture right away, then stir it all back into the pot.
Ladle into bowls and top with the scallion greens.

title: Creamy Miso-Hummus Udon with Crispy Pork
description: Thick, chewy udon tossed in a creamy miso, hummus and sesame sauce, topped with crispy hoisin-glazed pork, charred corn, scallions and sesame seeds. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: The starchy noodle water is what makes the sauce silky and clingy, so don't skip saving it. Contains sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 570 kcal, 19g fat, 59g carbs, 38g protein.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil. Trim and thinly slice the scallions, keeping the dark greens apart. Chop 3 large garlic cloves finely. Whisk the miso, hummus and 2 teaspoons sesame oil in a large bowl and keep the rest of the sesame oil for the pork.

Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a medium skillet over high heat until it smokes. Add the corn and cook, stirring now and then, until charred in spots, about 1 minute. Season and move to a plate. Heat another 2 teaspoons oil until smoking and cook the pork, breaking it up, until deeply browned, 5–7 minutes.

Add the scallion whites and light greens and the garlic and cook about 1 minute. Stir in the hoisin and the remaining sesame oil and cook, stirring often, until the pork is shiny and glazed, 1–2 minutes. Take off the heat, pour off extra fat if needed, and season.

Boil the udon, stirring to separate, 1–2 minutes. Save ½ cup of the water and drain. Add the noodles to the miso-hummus bowl and stir fast, adding the saved water a tablespoon at a time, until they are coated in a creamy sauce. Salt if needed.
Divide the noodles among bowls, top with the pork, corn, scallion greens and sesame seeds, and mix before eating.

title: Creamy Mushroom Chicken
description: Paprika-seasoned chicken breasts in a creamy mushroom and Dijon pan sauce over lemony mashed potatoes with spinach folded in. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk (cream cheese, butter). Per serving: about 640 kcal, 30g fat, 48g carbs, 48g protein.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks. Cover by 1 inch with salted water in a large pot, put the lid on and bring to a boil over high heat. Uncover and cook until fork-tender, 10–12 minutes.

Meanwhile, thinly slice 2 large garlic cloves and put the spinach in a colander. Add half the garlic to the potatoes for their last 2 minutes. Save ⅓ cup of the cooking water, then drain the potatoes over the spinach to wilt it. Return everything to the pot and cover.

Trim and thinly slice the mushrooms. Grate 1 teaspoon lemon zest and squeeze 2 teaspoons juice, keeping them separate; cut the rest of the lemon into wedges. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt, pepper and 1 teaspoon paprika. Stir all the broth concentrate and Dijon with 1¼ cups water in a measuring cup.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 4 minutes a side. Move to a plate. Add the mushrooms and 1½ tablespoons oil to the skillet, season, and cook until tender, 2–3 minutes. Stir in the rest of the garlic.

Pour in the broth mixture, bring to a boil and scrape up the browned bits, then let it reduce by half, 2–3 minutes. Turn to medium and whisk in the cream cheese and lemon juice until smooth. Season, return the chicken and its juices, and turn to coat. Cover.
Warm the potatoes over medium heat with the saved water, 2 tablespoons butter and the lemon zest, and mash until smooth. Serve the chicken and sauce over the potatoes with lemon wedges.

title: Crispy Chorizo-Potato Tacos
description: Hearty but not heavy: crisp pan-fried potatoes and chorizo in charred tortillas with a scallion pico de gallo and sour cream. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 730 kcal, 30g fat, 85g carbs, 36g protein.
instructions: Scrub the potatoes and cut them into ¼-inch pieces. Put them in a large heavy skillet, cast iron if you have it, with a big pinch of salt, 2 teaspoons vinegar and water to cover by 1 inch. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat, then uncover and cook until fork-tender, about 5 minutes. Drain and wipe out the skillet.

Meanwhile, trim and thinly slice the scallions, keeping the dark greens apart. Cut the tomatoes into ¼-inch pieces and chop 1 teaspoon garlic finely. Mix the tomatoes, garlic, half the dark scallion greens, 2 teaspoons each of vinegar and oil, and a big pinch each of salt and pepper in a medium bowl.

Thin all the sour cream with water a teaspoon at a time and season it. Heat the skillet over medium-high and char the tortillas one at a time on one side, about 30 seconds each. Keep them wrapped in a towel or foil.

Heat 3 tablespoons oil in the skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Add the potatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper, shake them into one layer, and cook, stirring now and then, until lightly browned all over, 3–5 minutes. Take the chorizo out of its casing if needed.

Add the chorizo and the scallion whites and light greens and cook, breaking up the meat, until the chorizo is cooked and the potatoes are crisp and golden, 5–7 minutes. Season. Fill the tortillas and top with the pico, sour cream and the rest of the scallion greens.

title: Crispy Firecracker Pork
description: Takeout at home: cornstarch-crisped pork tossed in a sticky sweet chili and gochugaru sauce, with rice, broccoli, peanuts and crispy onions. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains peanuts, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 920 kcal, 37g fat, 116g carbs, 40g protein.
instructions: Bring the rice, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat. Cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, about 17 minutes. Take off the heat and keep covered.
Heat ¼ inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pat the pork dry, season with salt and pepper, and toss with all the cornstarch in a medium bowl until coated.

When the oil shimmers and reaches 350°F (a pinch of cornstarch should sizzle straight away), add the pork in one layer, in batches if needed. Fry, turning now and then, until crisp and golden, 4–5 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Carefully pour the oil into a large heatproof bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Cut the broccoli into florets if needed and microwave, covered, until crisp-tender, 2–3 minutes. Season. Roughly chop the peanuts.

Heat 2 teaspoons oil in the skillet over medium heat and stir 2 teaspoons gochugaru (or more) until fragrant. Add all the Thai chili sauce and tamari and ¼ cup water and bring to a simmer. Lower to medium-low and season.

Toss the pork in the sauce, thinning with a tablespoon of water at a time if it is too thick. Season. Fluff the rice onto plates and top with the pork and broccoli, then the crispy onions and peanuts.

title: Crispy Lemon-Butter Chicken
description: Thin chicken breasts in a glossy lemon-butter sauce under a radicchio and arugula salad, dressed with the oil left from frying crispy shallots. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Cook the chicken to 165°F. Contains milk. Per serving: about 570 kcal, 36g fat, 21g carbs, 41g protein.
instructions: Trim the shallot and slice it into thin rounds. Heat ¼ cup oil in a small skillet over medium heat and fry the shallot until golden, 8–10 minutes. Lift it onto a paper towel with a slotted spoon and salt it. Keep the oil.
Meanwhile, put each chicken breast between sheets of plastic wrap and pound to ¼ inch with a mallet or heavy pan. Squeeze ⅓ cup lemon juice.
Stir ½ cup flour with 1½ teaspoons salt in a shallow dish and coat each breast, shaking off the extra.
Whisk the shallot oil with the Dijon, 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar and 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice, and season. Quarter and core the radicchio, chop it roughly, and toss it in the dressing.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches until golden, 2–3 minutes, then turn and cook 1–2 minutes more, until it reaches 165°F. Add oil if the pan gets dry. Put all the chicken back in the pan with 3 tablespoons butter and the rest of the lemon juice and cook until the sauce thickens and coats it, about 1 minute.
Grate the Parmesan if needed. Toss the arugula into the radicchio. Serve the chicken topped with the salad, Parmesan and crispy shallots.

title: Crispy Parm Chicken Tenders
description: Chicken strips in a nutty Parmesan-panko crust, pan-fried crisp, with roasted potato wedges, broccoli and a barbecue-ranch dip. A safe bet for picky eaters. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains egg, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 760 kcal, 35g fat, 68g carbs, 48g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into ¼-inch wedges. Toss them on 2 rimmed baking sheets with 2 tablespoons oil per sheet, season, and roast until golden underneath, about 20 minutes.
Cut the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed. Grate 1 teaspoon garlic into a medium bowl and beat in 1 large egg, 1 tablespoon water and ½ teaspoon salt.
Pat the chicken dry. Mix the panko and Parmesan in a shallow bowl and season. Dip the chicken in the egg, let the extra drip off, then press it into the crumbs and tap off the excess. Set on a plate.

Turn the potatoes and push them to one side of each sheet. Put the broccoli on the empty side, toss it with 1 tablespoon oil per sheet, and season. Roast until the broccoli is tender and browned in spots and the potatoes are crisp, 8–10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat ¼ inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of panko sizzles. Fry the chicken in batches, turning once, until golden and cooked through, 2–3 minutes a side, lowering the heat if it browns too fast. Drain on paper towels.
Whisk the mayonnaise, barbecue sauce and 1 tablespoon ranch seasoning in a small bowl. Serve the tenders with the vegetables and the dip.

title: Curried Coconut Chicken Stew
description: Chicken and sautéed peppers in a silky blended sauce of tomato, onion, ginger, curry powder and coconut milk, over rice with cilantro and lime. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk and tree nuts. Per serving: about 620 kcal, 14g fat, 80g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Bring the rice, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a small saucepan. Cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, about 17 minutes. Keep covered.

Grate 2 teaspoons each of ginger and garlic. Halve and roughly chop the onion. Cut the tomatoes into ½-inch pieces. Pick the cilantro leaves and set them aside; chop the stems finely. Whisk the coconut milk powder with 1¼ cups hot tap water and 2 teaspoons sugar in a measuring cup.

Pat the chicken dry and season it. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a medium Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on both sides, 5–7 minutes. Move it to a bowl. While it browns, seed the peppers and slice them into ½-inch strips.
Add another tablespoon of oil to the pot and cook the peppers, stirring now and then, until soft and browned, 5–7 minutes. Add them to the chicken.

Cook the onion and tomatoes in the pot, stirring as needed, until the tomatoes collapse and the onion softens, 5–7 minutes. Stir in the cilantro stems, ginger, garlic and curry powder until fragrant. Add the coconut milk, bring to a simmer, cover and cook 10 minutes. Season, then blend smooth with an immersion blender.
Return the chicken and peppers to the sauce and heat through. Cut the lime into wedges. Fluff the rice onto plates, spoon the stew over, and finish with cilantro leaves and a squeeze of lime.

title: Feta Burger & Onion Jam
description: A pub-style burger at home: seared beef patties on butter-toasted buns with sweet balsamic onion jam, a feta and garlic aioli spread and shredded lettuce, plus oven fries. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Press a shallow dent into the middle of each patty so it cooks flat instead of puffing up. Contains egg, milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 1630 kcal, 113g fat, 102g carbs, 51g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into ¼-inch fries. Toss with 3 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper, spread over 2 rimmed baking sheets, and roast until crisp and golden, 30–35 minutes, swapping the sheets halfway.

Halve and thinly slice the onions. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat until it foams. Add the onions and a pinch of salt, cover, and cook, stirring now and then, until they collapse to about half, 1–2 minutes. Uncover, turn to medium-low, and cook, stirring now and then, until soft and golden, 10–12 minutes.

If the onions darken too fast, add a tablespoon of water and scrape the pan. When they are soft and golden, stir in the tamari and 2 tablespoons each of brown sugar and balsamic vinegar and cook until jammy, 2–3 minutes more. Spoon into a bowl, then wash the skillet.

While the onions cook, grate 1 teaspoon garlic into a small bowl and stir in the mayonnaise with a little salt and pepper. In another small bowl, mash the feta with half the garlic aioli until spreadable but still a bit chunky. Halve the lettuce and slice it thin.

Shape the beef into 4 patties about 4 inches wide, press a dent into one side of each, and season both sides. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in the skillet over medium heat and toast the buns cut side down, swirling them in the butter, until golden, 1–2 minutes. Wipe out the skillet.
