Heat 2 tablespoons oil in the skillet until it just smokes. Cook the patties dent side up until browned and medium rare, 2–3 minutes a side, or longer if you like. Spread onion jam on the bottom buns and add the burgers, feta spread and lettuce. Serve with the fries and the rest of the aioli.

title: French Onion Beef Stroganoff
description: French onion soup meets stroganoff in one skillet: ground beef, mushrooms, browned onion and egg noodles in a savory sauce, broiled under two cheeses. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains egg, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 990 kcal, 50g fat, 72g carbs, 53g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Halve the onion and cut it into ½-inch pieces. Wipe the mushrooms, trim the stems, and slice the caps ¼ inch thick. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Roughly chop the parsley leaves and tender stems. Grate the Parmesan finely.
Cook the noodles, stirring now and then, until al dente, 4–5 minutes. Drain and toss with a little oil so they don't stick.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large ovenproof skillet over high heat. Add the onion and mushrooms, season, and cook, stirring, until tender and browned in spots, 6–7 minutes. Lower to medium if they brown too fast. Move them to a bowl.

Set a rack 6 inches below the broiler and turn it on. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and garlic, season, and cook, breaking it up, until deeply browned and cooked through, 5–6 minutes. Pour off excess fat. Stir in 2 tablespoons flour for 1 minute.

Return the mushrooms and onion, add the broth concentrate and 1⅔ cups water, and scrape up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer, then stir in the noodles, half the parsley and 3 tablespoons butter. Take off the heat, season, and cover with both cheeses.
Broil until the cheese melts and browns in places, 3–4 minutes, watching closely. Let it stand 5 minutes and scatter over the rest of the parsley.

title: French Onion Chicken Breast
description: Seared chicken breasts in a thyme pan sauce, piled with caramelized onions and melted cheese like French onion soup, with garlic-rubbed toast and a spinach salad. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 590 kcal, 30g fat, 34g carbs, 51g protein.
instructions: Thinly slice the onions. Heat 1 tablespoon each of butter and oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onions, 2 teaspoons sugar and a pinch of salt and pepper, and cook, stirring, until deeply browned, 12–15 minutes, adding a tablespoon of water and scraping whenever the pan browns. Move to a bowl and wipe out the skillet.

Meanwhile, slice 2 large garlic cloves thin and keep a third clove whole. Halve the baguette lengthwise and cut each half into 4 pieces. Drizzle the cut sides with oil and season. Pick and finely chop the thyme leaves.

Set a rack at the top of the oven and turn on the broiler. Pat the chicken dry and season it. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until well browned and cooked through, 3–4 minutes a side. Move to a plate.

Add the sliced garlic and 2 teaspoons oil to the skillet and stir until lightly golden, about 30 seconds. Add the thyme, broth concentrate and ¾ cup water and simmer, scraping up the browned bits, until slightly thickened, about 2 minutes. Put the chicken back and top it with the onions and cheese.

Broil the skillet on the top rack until the cheese is melted and golden, 2–4 minutes, watching closely, then take it out carefully. Broil the bread right on the rack until toasted, 1–2 minutes a side, and rub the cut sides with the whole garlic clove.
Whisk 2 tablespoons oil, 1 tablespoon vinegar, 1½ teaspoons Dijon and a pinch of sugar in a medium bowl and season. Toss in the spinach. Serve the chicken with the salad and garlic toast.

title: Gochujang Buttered Noodles
description: A fast pantry dinner: spaghetti in a garlicky, brick-red butter sauce of gochujang mellowed with honey and sherry vinegar, sweet, savory and tangy at once. Any noodle works. Adapted from Eric Kim.
notes:
About 25 minutes. Buy plain gochujang paste, not gochujang sauce, which has vinegar and sugar added. Oil the measuring spoon first and the paste slides right out.

For one serving: 4 to 5 ounces fresh or instant ramen noodles, 1½ tablespoons butter (1 for the garlic, ½ for the end), 3 garlic cloves, 1 heaping tablespoon gochujang, 1 tablespoon honey and 1 tablespoon sherry or rice vinegar. Cut each cook time by 1 to 2 minutes.
instructions: Boil the spaghetti in a large pot following the package. Save 1 cup of the water, drain, and return the pasta to the pot.
Meanwhile, melt 4 tablespoons of the butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic with plenty of salt and cook, stirring now and then, until it softens without browning, 1 to 3 minutes.

Stir in the gochujang, honey and vinegar and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Keep stirring until it reduces a lot, 3 to 4 minutes; a spatula dragged across the pan should leave a line that holds for about 3 seconds. Take off the heat.

Scrape the sauce into the pasta, add the last 2 tablespoons butter, and stir hard until it melts. Loosen with splashes of the pasta water as needed and season with salt and pepper. Top with cilantro or scallions if you have them and eat right away.

title: Beef & Refried Bean Tacos
description: Quick tacos of cumin and chili-spiced beef with browned onion over warm refried beans, topped with pickled onion, radish, cilantro and crema. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: No microwave? Warm the beans in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, wipe it out, then heat the tortillas one or two at a time, about 1 minute a side. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 900 kcal, 39g fat, 82g carbs, 47g protein.
instructions: Halve the onion and slice it thin crosswise. In a small bowl, mix ⅓ cup of it with 1½ tablespoons vinegar and a pinch each of salt and sugar, and leave it to pickle.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef, the rest of the onion and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat and stirring now and then, until deeply browned and cooked through, 8–10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the lime into wedges and slice the radishes thin. Stir all the sour cream with 2 tablespoons water in a small bowl and season.

Add all the cumin and 2 teaspoons chili powder (more if you like heat) to the beef and stir for about 30 seconds. Add ½ cup water, scrape up the browned bits, and simmer until reduced by two thirds, about 1 minute. Take off the heat and season.

Microwave the refried beans in a medium bowl until hot, about 2 minutes, and stir in the juice of 1 lime wedge. Wrap the tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave until warm, 30–60 seconds. Pick the cilantro leaves.
Spread beans on the tortillas, add the beef, and top with pickled onion, radish, cilantro and crema. Serve with the rest of the lime.

title: Beef & Bean Chili
description: A fast chili of ground beef, kidney beans, peppers and onion in a taco-spiced tomato sauce, over cilantro rice with sour cream. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk (sour cream). Per serving: about 890 kcal, 27g fat, 97g carbs, 44g protein.
instructions: Bring the rice, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt to a boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, about 17 minutes. Keep covered off the heat.
Chop all the onion finely. Seed the peppers and cut them into ½-inch pieces.

Heat ¼ cup oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef, peppers, all the taco seasoning and three quarters of the onion. Cook, stirring now and then, until the beef is cooked and the vegetables are soft, 5–7 minutes.

Stir in ½ cup tomato paste and cook until it turns brick red, about 1 minute. Add the broth concentrate, the beans with their liquid and ⅔ cup water. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat, then uncover and season. Cover to keep warm.
Chop the cilantro leaves and tender stems finely. Fluff the rice and stir in the cilantro.
Serve the chili over the rice with sour cream and the rest of the onion if you like.

title: Grilled Harissa Chicken with Fattoush Salad
description: Harissa-marinated grilled chicken over a fattoush-style salad of grilled za'atar pita, tomato, cucumber, onion and romaine, with a charred lemon tahini dressing, mint and feta. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: No grill? Use a grill pan on high. Contains milk, sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 610 kcal, 34g fat, 33g carbs, 47g protein.
instructions: Heat a grill to high if you're using one. Mix the harissa spice with ¼ cup olive oil and a big pinch of salt in a large bowl. Pat the chicken dry, toss it in the mixture, and leave it to marinate.
Stir all but 1 tablespoon of the za'atar into ⅓ cup oil and brush it over the pita.
If you're using a grill pan, heat it on high now. Grill the pita until charred, 2–3 minutes a side. Let it cool, then tear or cut it into 1-inch pieces.
Zest the lemon, cut it in half, and grill it cut side down until charred and juicy, 5–7 minutes.
Grate 1 teaspoon garlic into a small bowl. Squeeze one charred lemon half into another small bowl and cut the other half into wedges.
Stir the tahini, the remaining za'atar, 2 tablespoons of the charred lemon juice, 1 tablespoon lemon zest and 1 teaspoon sugar into the garlic, adding water until it pours.
Grill the chicken until charred and cooked through, 3–5 minutes a side, and let it rest.
Meanwhile, halve and thinly slice the onion. Cut the tomatoes into ½-inch pieces. Peel and seed the cucumber if you like and cut it into ½-inch pieces. Slice the romaine thin, discarding the ends.
Put the vegetables and pita in a large bowl, drizzle with oil and the rest of the lemon juice, season, and toss.
Roughly chop the mint leaves and slice the chicken thin.
Plate the salad, top with the chicken and mint, drizzle with the tahini dressing, crumble over the feta, and serve with the lemon wedges.

title: Grilled Pesto Chicken
description: Pesto-brushed grilled chicken with a panzanella of charred zucchini, garlic-rubbed grilled bread, tomatoes and mozzarella in an Italian vinaigrette. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. A grill pan works fine. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 610 kcal, 30g fat, 30g carbs, 58g protein.
instructions: Heat a grill or grill pan to high and oil the grates. Trim the zucchini, halve it lengthwise, rub with oil, and season with 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning and a pinch of salt and pepper. Split the rolls if needed. Peel and smash 1 garlic clove.

Grill the zucchini, covered, turning now and then, until tender and charred in spots, 10–12 minutes. Drizzle the cut sides of the bread with oil and grill, turning once, until charred in spots, 2–3 minutes a side. Rub the bread with the smashed garlic right away and salt it.

Meanwhile, cut the tomatoes and mozzarella into ¾-inch pieces. Whisk 2 tablespoons oil, 1 tablespoon vinegar and 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning in a large bowl, season, and toss in the tomatoes and mozzarella. Spoon half the pesto into a small bowl for serving.

Pat the chicken dry and season it. Grill over high heat until browned and nearly done, 2–3 minutes a side. Brush with the rest of the pesto and grill, turning, until charred in spots and cooked through, about 1 minute more a side.
Once cool enough to handle, cut the zucchini and bread into ¾-inch pieces and toss them with the tomatoes and cheese.
Serve the chicken with the panzanella and drizzle with the saved pesto.

title: Grilled Za’atar Chicken With Garlic Yogurt and Cilantro
description: Chicken thighs made tender in a garlicky yogurt, za'atar and herb marinade, grilled or broiled until charred, with a lemony garlic yogurt sauce. Great with flatbread and a cucumber-tomato salad. Adapted from NYT Cooking.
notes: Marinate anywhere from 2 hours to overnight. Breasts work instead of thighs, but they cook faster, so watch them. If broiling, line the pan with foil for easy cleanup; not parchment, which can burn.
instructions: Stir 5 of the grated garlic cloves, half the lemon zest, ⅓ cup yogurt, the cilantro, oil, za'atar, oregano or marjoram, salt and pepper together in a large bowl or container. Add the chicken and toss to coat. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight.

Heat the grill to medium, or set a rack 3 inches below the broiler and turn it on. Shake the extra marinade off the chicken and cook until charred in spots, 5 to 8 minutes. Turn and cook another 5 to 8 minutes, until just done.
Meanwhile, stir the last grated garlic clove and the rest of the zest into the remaining ⅔ cup yogurt and season. Halve one of the zested lemons for serving and keep the other for another day.
Arrange the chicken on a platter, drizzle with olive oil and a good squeeze of lemon, scatter over cilantro and oregano or marjoram sprigs, and serve with the yogurt sauce.

title: Hickory-Smoked Barbecue Pulled Pork Sandwiches
description: A 4-pound pork butt in a spicy homemade rub, smoked low and slow over hickory, mopped with a thick bourbon barbecue sauce, then pulled and piled on buns. Adapted from Fork Knife Swoon.
notes: About 7 hours. The rub covers a 4-pound boneless pork butt and can go on up to 12 hours ahead. Plan on roughly 1½ hours of smoking per pound at 225°F, until the center reaches 200°F. Don't skip the 30-minute to 1-hour rest in foil.
instructions: For the rub, mix the dry ingredients with a fork or whisk.
Add the mustard and keep mixing until smooth.
Spread it thickly over every side of the pork. You can do this up to 12 hours before smoking.
Set the pork in an aluminum pan and leave it on the counter until it no longer feels cold.
Give it another generous coat of the rub.
Light the hickory. A charcoal chimney with crumpled newspaper underneath gets it going easily.
Once it is burning well, tip the wood into the smoker box. Charcoal briquettes can be added now to stretch the hickory; all wood works too, but costs more.
Close the smoker box so the smoke flows into the main chamber, and keep the side vent on the box open for air.
Put the pork, still in its pan, on the grill.
Push a probe thermometer into the thickest, coldest part of the meat.
Every 30 to 60 minutes, baste the pork with half of the sauce, as needed to keep the outside moist. A dark crust will form anyway; that's what keeps the inside juicy.
As soon as the center reaches 200°F, take the pork off. It will be very hot, so handle it carefully.
Lift it out of the pan and wrap it in two layers of heavy-duty foil. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes and up to an hour so the juices settle.
Unwrap it carefully, pull it into shreds with a fork, and gently mix in the rest of the sauce.
Pile the pork onto burger buns or any rolls you like.

title: Japanese-Inspired Glazed Pork Meatballs
description: Ginger-garlic pork meatballs in a sticky, sweet-savory stir-fry glaze, with roasted broccoli and peppers over rice, finished with sesame seeds and togarashi. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains egg, sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 940 kcal, 50g fat, 87g carbs, 41g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F. Bring the rice and 2 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan, then cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, 17–20 minutes. Keep covered.

Grate 2 teaspoons each of ginger and garlic. Seed the peppers and cut them into ½-inch strips. Cut the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed. Mix the pork, panko, half the ginger and garlic, 2 eggs, 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper in a medium bowl, and roll into 20 meatballs of about 2 tablespoons each.
Toss the broccoli and peppers on a rimmed baking sheet with the rest of the ginger and garlic, 3 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper. Roast until tender and browned at the edges, 15–20 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the meatballs, in batches if needed, turning as they brown, until seared and cooked through, 6–8 minutes.
With all the meatballs in the pan, add the stir-fry sauce, 4 tablespoons water and 1 teaspoon vinegar. Bring to a simmer and turn the meatballs to coat. Season to taste.
Fluff the rice onto plates and top with the vegetables and meatballs. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and as much togarashi as you like.

title: Marry Me Chicken
description: The viral favorite: golden chicken cutlets in a creamy, garlicky sauce with sun-dried tomatoes and Parmesan, sharpened with tomato paste. Adapted from Naz Deravian.
notes: About 1 hour. Twenty minutes in the freezer makes the breasts much easier to slice into cutlets. Serve with crusty bread and a sharp green salad, or over pasta, rice or polenta.
instructions: If using breasts, slice each one in half horizontally, starting at the thick end, to make 6 cutlets in all. Season both sides well with salt and pepper.
Spread the flour on a large plate, coat the cutlets and shake off the extra. Lay them out in a single layer.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. When hot, lower to medium and add the butter. As soon as it melts, add the cutlets and cook until golden, about 5 minutes. Turn and cook the other side until golden, 4 to 5 minutes. Work in batches if needed, adding more oil. Move to a plate.
Turn the heat to low and stir the garlic until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomato paste and stir until it darkens, about 2 minutes. Add oregano and red pepper flakes to taste.
Raise the heat to medium, pour in the stock, and simmer while scraping up the browned bits until reduced by half, about 5 minutes.

Stir in ½ cup of the cream and keep at a gentle simmer, lowering the heat if needed, until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the Parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes, add more cream if you like, and season.
Put the chicken back in the sauce to warm through, about 4 minutes. Take off the heat and scatter over the basil.

title: Meatball & Cannellini Bean Stew
description: Garlicky beef meatballs simmered in marinara with cannellini beans, spinach and Parmesan, finished with pesto and crunchy toasted panko. Italian flavors, no pasta. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains egg, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 830 kcal, 46g fat, 43g carbs, 48g protein.
instructions: Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Drain the beans and rinse under cold water. Grate the Parmesan finely.
Mix the beef, garlic, ½ cup panko, 2 large eggs, 2 teaspoons salt and some pepper in a medium bowl until well combined. Roll into 16 meatballs of about 2 tablespoons each.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Toast the rest of the panko, stirring now and then, until golden, 3–5 minutes, and tip it into a bowl.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat and brown the meatballs, turning them, 6–8 minutes. Pour off the extra oil and lower to medium. Add the marinara and ⅓ cup water and simmer, turning the meatballs every minute or so, until cooked through, 3–5 minutes. Move the meatballs to a plate and cover.
Add the beans, half the Parmesan and ⅓ cup water to the sauce and bring to a simmer. Stir in the spinach until wilted and season.
Spoon the beans and sauce into shallow bowls, add the meatballs, and drizzle with pesto. Top with the toasted panko and the rest of the Parmesan.

title: Mexican Street Corn Chicken Salad
description: Street corn turned into dinner: lime-marinated chicken and charred corn over spinach with radish, sunflower seeds, feta and cilantro, and a lime crema made from the same marinade. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains egg, milk and soy. Per serving: about 730 kcal, 55g fat, 23g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Chop 1 teaspoon garlic finely. Zest both limes into a medium bowl, then juice one and cut the other into wedges. Stir in the garlic, 3 tablespoons oil, 2 teaspoons Tex-Mex spice, 1 teaspoon salt and some pepper.

Whisk all the mayonnaise with 2 tablespoons of the marinade in a small bowl, adding 2–3 teaspoons water until creamy. Season and set aside. Pat the chicken dry and toss it in the rest of the marinade.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in one layer and leave it until browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Stir and cook until done, about 2 minutes more. Move to a board to cool a little.
Put the skillet back on high heat. When it is very hot, spread the corn in one layer and leave it until charred underneath, 2–3 minutes. Stir, cook 1 minute more, and season.

Slice the radish thin. Toss the spinach in a large bowl with the juice of 2 lime wedges, a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt. Top with the chicken, corn, radish and sunflower seeds, then crumble over the feta and tear over the cilantro. Drizzle with the crema and serve with the remaining lime.

title: Miso Pork Tsukemen (Dipping Ramen) with Spinach
description: Dipping ramen: chilled noodles, gingery soy-glazed pork and garlic spinach served beside a small bowl of hot, concentrated miso broth for dunking. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Keeping the noodles out of the broth keeps them chewy and the broth strong. Contains sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 720 kcal, 26g fat, 87g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil. Cook the noodles, stirring now and then so they don't clump, until al dente, 4–5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with 2 teaspoons neutral oil. Keep the saucepan.

Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely and grate 1 tablespoon ginger. Trim and thinly slice the scallions, keeping the dark greens apart. Whisk 2 cups water with the miso, pork ramen base and 2 teaspoons each of vinegar and sugar in a measuring cup, then sprinkle the gelatin over. Pat the pork dry and toss it with the tamari, half the ginger, 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon salt.

Heat 1 tablespoon neutral oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Stir half the garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute, then add the spinach and cook until wilted, 1–2 minutes. Stir in 1 teaspoon sesame oil, season, and move to a plate.
Heat 1 tablespoon neutral oil in the skillet over high heat. Spread the pork in one layer and leave it until the edges brown, 2–3 minutes. Stir and cook until done, 1–2 minutes more.

In the saucepan, cook the scallion whites and light greens with the rest of the garlic and ginger in 2 tablespoons neutral oil over medium-high heat, stirring, until fragrant, 1–2 minutes. Add the miso mixture, bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the remaining sesame oil.
Put the noodles, pork and spinach in bowls and the hot broth in small separate bowls, topped with scallion greens. Dip as you eat.

title: Pan-Roasted Chicken & Caramelized Onions
description: Seared chicken breasts under a caramelized onion pan sauce, with roasted potato wedges and broccoli tossed in Parmesan-garlic butter like garlic knots. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk (Parmesan, butter). Per serving: about 760 kcal, 40g fat, 55g carbs, 48g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into wedges. Toss with 1½ tablespoons oil, salt and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet, then move half to a second sheet. Roast on both racks until deep golden underneath, 20–25 minutes. Slice the onion into ¼-inch rings.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, season, cover, and cook until soft, 5–6 minutes. Uncover and cook, stirring, until deeply browned, 8–10 minutes, adding a tablespoon of water whenever it sticks. Move to a bowl and wipe out the skillet.

Grate the Parmesan and ½ teaspoon garlic finely into a medium bowl. Pick and finely chop the parsley leaves. Add 4 tablespoons butter and half the parsley to the bowl and leave it to soften. Cut the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed.

Turn the potatoes and push them to one side of each sheet. Add the broccoli to the empty side, drizzle with oil, and season. Roast until the broccoli is browned in spots and the potatoes are crisp, 5–8 minutes. Mash the butter mixture together with a fork and toss it with the potatoes and broccoli right on the sheets.

While the vegetables roast, pat the chicken dry, pound it to an even ½ inch, and season with the steak seasoning. Heat 1½ tablespoons oil in the skillet over medium-high heat and cook until browned and done, 3–4 minutes a side. Move to a plate and cover.

Put the onion, broth concentrate, 1 cup water, 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon vinegar in the skillet and bring to a boil. Lower to medium-low and cook, stirring, until slightly reduced, 3–4 minutes. Spoon the onions and sauce over the chicken, sprinkle with the rest of the parsley, and serve with the potatoes and broccoli.

title: Parmesan-Lemon Chicken
description: Chicken breasts roasted under a Parmesan and lemon zest crust, with a bright blended pea, spinach and herb purée and toasted orzo with spinach. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 570 kcal, 22g fat, 42g carbs, 52g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Warm 2 teaspoons oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat and toast the orzo, stirring, 2–3 minutes. Add the broth concentrate, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn down to a simmer, and cook until tender and the liquid is gone, 12–15 minutes. Keep covered off the heat.

Microwave the peas in a medium bowl until bright green and tender, about 1 minute. Zest the lemon, then halve it and squeeze 1 tablespoon juice. Grate the Parmesan if needed. Roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Mix 1 teaspoon lemon zest with ¼ cup Parmesan in a small bowl.

Pat the chicken dry and season it. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken well on one side. Turn it, press the Parmesan-lemon mixture on top, and roast on the upper rack until browned and cooked through, 5–7 minutes.

Blend the peas, lemon juice, the rest of the Parmesan and zest, and 2 tablespoons each of oil and water until about as thick as hummus. Add the cilantro and 2 packed cups spinach and blend until smooth. Season.
Stir the remaining spinach and a squeeze of lemon into the orzo until wilted, and season. Serve the chicken with the pea purée and orzo.

title: Pasta Alla Norma
description: The Sicilian classic: soft, browned eggplant in a garlicky tomato and oregano sauce, tossed with pasta and topped with ricotta salata. A filling vegetarian dinner in under an hour. Adapted from Mark Bittman.
notes: About 45 minutes.
instructions: Slice the eggplant about ½ inch thick. Fry it in plenty of olive oil without crowding the pan, salting as you go and adding oil as needed. It will take a few batches; let each one get properly brown and soft. Set the slices on a plate (not on paper towels). Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

When the eggplant is done, you want about two tablespoons of oil left in the pan; pour some off or add a little. Over medium heat, cook the garlic and chiles until the garlic just colors. Add the tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper and cook, stirring now and then, until saucy but not dry.

Cook the pasta until just tender. While it cooks, cut the eggplant into strips and warm it in the sauce for a minute. Drain the pasta, toss it with the sauce and eggplant, and adjust the seasoning. Finish with parsley or basil and the grated cheese.

title: Pasta all'Amatriciana
description: Spaghetti in a tangy, gently spicy sauce of crisp bacon, soft onion, marinara and crushed red pepper, finished with plenty of Parmesan. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 760 kcal, 34g fat, 76g carbs, 37g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cut the bacon into ¼-inch pieces. Chop the onion and 2 large garlic cloves finely. Pick and finely chop the parsley leaves. Grate three quarters of the Parmesan finely.

Put the bacon, onion and 2 tablespoons oil in a second large pot over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring often, until the bacon is crisp and golden and the onion soft, 10–12 minutes, turning the heat down if the onion browns before the bacon is done. Add the garlic and crushed red pepper and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the marinara and ½ cup water and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened, about 10 minutes. Season to taste.

Halfway through the sauce, start the pasta and cook until just short of al dente, 7–8 minutes. Save 1½ cups of the water and drain. Add the pasta and 1 cup of the water to the sauce and toss hard over high heat until the pasta is al dente and the sauce clings, 1–2 minutes.
Off the heat, toss in the grated Parmesan and parsley. Loosen with more pasta water a tablespoon at a time if you like, and season.
Divide into bowls, grate the rest of the Parmesan over, add a drizzle of oil if you like, and serve right away.

title: Pork & Rice Enchilada Casserole
description: A no-fuss tray bake of pulled pork, rice, black beans, green chiles and enchilada sauce under melted cheese. Mix, cover and bake. Adapted from Martha Stewart and Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk. Per serving: about 880 kcal, 44g fat, 75g carbs, 32g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle.
Trim and thinly slice the scallions. Rinse and drain the beans. Pat the pork dry and pull it into bite-size pieces.
In a large bowl, mix the pork, rice, beans, enchilada sauce, green chiles, taco seasoning, most of the scallions and half the cheese. Season to taste.

Spread it in the foil tray, cover with the rest of the cheese, and cover with foil. Set the tray on a rimmed baking sheet and bake on the middle rack until the cheese melts and the rice is hot all the way through, 30–35 minutes.
Scatter the saved scallions over before serving.

title: Prosciutto-Mozzarella Panini
description: A 15-minute pressed sandwich of prosciutto, mozzarella, roasted red peppers and pesto, griddled until the cheese melts. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Under 20 minutes. Short on time? Toast the rolls first and skip pressing. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 530 kcal, 29g fat, 43g carbs, 27g protein.
instructions: Slice the mozzarella thin.
Spread pesto on the cut sides of the rolls and fill each with mozzarella, peppers and prosciutto.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the sandwiches, pressing down on them now and then, until the cheese melts, 3–4 minutes a side.
Serve hot.

title: Red Lentil Soup
description: A light, spicy red lentil soup in the style of Turkish mercimek çorbası, half blended so it's neither chunky nor smooth, with lemon cutting the cumin and chile. Under an hour. Adapted from Melissa Clark.
notes: About 45 minutes. You'll need 2 cups water along with the broth; it isn't in the ingredient list.
instructions: Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large pot over high heat until it shimmers. Cook the onion and garlic until golden, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, chili powder and ¼ teaspoon each of salt and pepper, and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the broth, 2 cups water, the lentils and the carrot. Bring to a simmer, set the lid ajar, and turn to medium-low. Cook until the lentils are soft, about 30 minutes. Salt to taste.
Blend half the soup with an immersion blender, blender or food processor and stir it back in. It should stay a little chunky.
Reheat if needed, then stir in the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve with a drizzle of good olive oil and a pinch of chili powder if you like.

title: Roast Chicken Marbella
description: A quick take on the classic: pounded chicken breasts braised in a sweet and briny sauce of figs, olives and garlic, with crisp rosemary roast potatoes for mopping it up. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains milk (butter). Per serving: about 700 kcal, 32g fat, 63g carbs, 45g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Pat the chicken dry, put it between sheets of plastic, and pound to an even ½ inch. Toss it in a large bowl with 2 tablespoons each of oil and vinegar and a big pinch each of salt, pepper and sugar. Leave it at room temperature.

Strip the rosemary leaves and chop them finely. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Toss on a rimmed baking sheet with the rosemary, ¼ cup oil and a big pinch of salt and pepper. Roast on the lower rack without stirring until golden and tender, about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop ½ cup onion and 3 large garlic cloves finely. Quarter the figs. Roughly chop the olives, removing any pits.

When the potatoes have had 10 minutes, heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until golden underneath, about 3 minutes, and move it to a plate. It won't be cooked through.

Straight away, cook the onion in the skillet, stirring, until soft and lightly browned, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic, olives and figs for about 1 minute. Stir in the broth concentrate and ¾ cup water, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a simmer. Put the chicken back, browned side up, with its juices.

Move the skillet to the upper rack and cook until the chicken is done and the sauce has thickened a little, 7–10 minutes. Take it out carefully and swirl in 2 tablespoons butter. Chop the parsley, leaves and stems. Serve the chicken with the sauce spooned over, the potatoes alongside, and parsley on top.

title: Seared Chicken & Apple-Shallot Pan Sauce
description: Chicken breasts simmered in a sweet-savory apple, shallot and Dijon pan sauce, with creamy mashed sweet potatoes and a spinach and pecan salad. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk and tree nuts. Per serving: about 810 kcal, 52g fat, 43g carbs, 45g protein.
instructions: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Cover by 1 inch with salted water in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil, and simmer until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain, return to the pot and cover.

Chop the shallot finely. Core the apple and cut it into ¼-inch cubes. Pat the chicken dry and season it. Whisk 2 tablespoons oil with 1 tablespoon each of vinegar and chopped shallot in a medium bowl for the salad.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken well on both sides, 2–3 minutes a side. It won't be cooked through. Move it to a plate.

Melt 1 packet of the garlic herb butter in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the apples and the rest of the shallot, stirring now and then, until well browned and a little soft, 3–5 minutes. Stir in 2 teaspoons flour for about 30 seconds.

Add the turkey broth concentrate, 2 teaspoons Dijon and 1½ cups water and bring to a simmer, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken and simmer over medium-low heat until it is cooked through, the apples are tender and the sauce has thickened, 5–7 minutes.

Toast the pecans if you like. Set the sweet potatoes over medium-high heat, add the sour cream and the rest of the butter, and mash. Season. Toss the spinach and pecans with the dressing. Serve the chicken with the apples and sauce over it, and the mash and salad alongside.

title: Sesame Beef Stir-Fry
description: A fast noodle stir-fry of garlicky ground beef, spinach and scallions in a sesame stir-fry sauce, quicker than takeout. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 760 kcal, 22g fat, 87g carbs, 39g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Thinly slice 2 large garlic cloves. Trim the scallions and cut them into ½-inch pieces.
Whisk all the stir-fry sauce with 6 tablespoons water and 2 teaspoons each of oil and vinegar in a small bowl. Cut the limes into wedges.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over high heat. Add the beef and garlic, season, and cook, breaking it into large pieces, until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Take off the heat and spoon off any extra fat.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles, stirring, until al dente, 3–5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain again.
Add the spinach and scallions to the beef and stir over medium heat until the spinach just wilts, about 1 minute.
Add the noodles, sauce and half the sesame seeds and toss until coated, about 1 minute. Season, sprinkle with the rest of the sesame seeds, and squeeze lime over.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
description: Fajitas without the stovetop splatter: peppers, poblanos and onion roasted until charred, chili-spiced chicken broiled on the same pan, all wrapped in warm tortillas. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: No microwave? Toast the tortillas one at a time in a skillet over medium-high heat, about 30 seconds a side, and wrap them in foil or a towel. Contains milk, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 740 kcal, 34g fat, 70g carbs, 45g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Seed the bell and poblano peppers and cut them into ½-inch strips. Halve the onion and cut it into ½-inch slices through the root.

Toss the peppers and onion on a rimmed baking sheet with 3 tablespoons oil and a big pinch each of salt and pepper, and spread them out. Roast on the upper rack until tender and lightly charred, 15–20 minutes. Then turn the oven to broil.

Meanwhile, quarter the lime and roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems; set both aside. Pat the chicken dry and toss it in a medium bowl with the chili powder, 2 tablespoons oil and 1 teaspoon salt.
Move the roasted vegetables to a platter. Spread the chicken on the sheet and broil on the upper rack until cooked through, 3–5 minutes, watching closely.
Stack the tortillas on a plate, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave in 30-second bursts until warm.
Fill the tortillas with vegetables and chicken and top with sour cream, salsa, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Shrimp & Chorizo Paella
description: An oven-baked paella of arborio rice with chorizo, sweet peppers and smoked paprika in seafood broth, topped with shrimp and peas, crisped on the stove at the end and served with garlic aioli. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 40–50 minutes. Contains egg, fish, shellfish and soy. Per serving: about 910 kcal, 40g fat, 84g carbs, 55g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Chop the onions and 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Set aside half the parsley leaves; chop the rest with the stems. Trim the peppers and slice them into ¼-inch rings. Cut the lemon into 8 wedges. Rinse the shrimp (thaw them under cool running water if needed), pat dry, and season with salt, pepper and 2 teaspoons paprika.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large heavy ovenproof skillet, cast iron if you have it, over medium-high heat. Cook the chorizo, breaking it up, until browned in spots and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Lift it into a bowl with a slotted spoon. Cook the onion and half the peppers in the same pan, stirring, until soft, 5–8 minutes.

Stir in ¼ cup tomato paste and cook until it darkens, about 2 minutes. Add 2 teaspoons each of the chopped garlic and paprika for about 30 seconds. Add the rice, chorizo and 1½ tablespoons oil and stir for about 30 seconds. Whisk all the broth concentrate with 3½ cups water.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the broth, half the chopped parsley, the rest of the peppers and 1½ teaspoons salt. Set the lemon wedges cut side up in a ring around the edge. Bring to a boil and cook without stirring, 3–4 minutes. Cover with foil and bake on the middle rack until the liquid is nearly absorbed and the rice almost tender, about 12 minutes.

Uncover, scatter the shrimp and peas over the top, cover again, and bake until the shrimp are cooked, about 3 minutes. Rest, covered, 5 minutes. Meanwhile, stir the mayo with the rest of the chopped parsley and garlic and 2 teaspoons water, and season.

Set the skillet over medium heat, uncovered, and turn it now and then so it browns evenly, until the bottom smells toasty, 4–7 minutes. Off the heat, salt it and scatter over the saved parsley leaves. Serve with the aioli.

title: Skillet Chicken Parm
description: Chicken Parm made weeknight-easy in one pan: no breading, just seared chicken baked under a quick, fresh tomato sauce with garlic, chili and oregano and lots of melted cheese. Adapted from The Dinner Plan.
notes:
Small breasts work best for the timing and the balance of chicken to sauce. If yours are large, pound them to about ½ inch.

Make ahead: assemble up to the cheese, then cover and chill for up to a day. Let it sit out about 20 minutes and bake uncovered. This beats reheating, since breasts dry out easily; if you do reheat portions, keep them covered in a 350°F oven or the microwave and go gently.

Serving at different times: it holds, covered, in a 200°F oven for about an hour, or keep it on the back of the stove next to a pot of spaghetti.

Also good in a hoagie roll with the sauce spooned over, wrapped in foil for eating on the go.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Heat the oil in a large high-sided sauté pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Season the chicken well, add it to the pan, and cook until lightly golden, about 2 minutes. Turn and cook 1 minute more.

Scatter the garlic around the chicken, then the pepper flakes and oregano. Pour the tomatoes over evenly, season, and shake the pan gently (or use a spoon) to spread the sauce. Top the chicken with as much mozzarella and Parmesan as you like.

Bake until the sauce bubbles and the chicken is just done, 12 to 14 minutes, then broil to brown if you like. Tear any basil over the top. Rest about 5 minutes before serving, and cover the hot handle with an oven mitt so nobody grabs it. Pass extra Parmesan.

title: Skillet Jumbo Shrimp & Orzo with Tomatoes & Feta
description: A one-skillet, Greek-leaning dinner: seared garlicky shrimp folded into orzo simmered with canned and sun-dried tomatoes, topped with feta and parsley. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk, shellfish and wheat. Per serving: about 650 kcal, 19g fat, 87g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Rinse the shrimp and pat them very dry. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic and the sun-dried tomatoes finely. In a large bowl, mix half the garlic with 1 teaspoon Tuscan spice, 2 tablespoons oil and 1 teaspoon salt, and toss the shrimp in it.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp, stirring now and then, until well browned and just done, 3–5 minutes. Move to a plate and wipe out the pan.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in the skillet over medium heat. Stir the sun-dried tomatoes, the rest of the Tuscan spice and the rest of the garlic until fragrant, 1–2 minutes. Add all the orzo and toast it, stirring, 1–2 minutes. Add all the canned tomatoes, breaking them up with a spoon.

Stir in 3 cups water and 1½ teaspoons salt and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Lower to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the orzo is al dente and most of the water is absorbed, 8–10 minutes. Stir in the shrimp to warm through, 1–2 minutes, and season.
Roughly chop the parsley and crumble the feta into big pieces.
Serve the orzo topped with the feta and parsley.

title: Slow Cooker Bolognese
description: A rich, hands-off ragù of beef, pork, tomatoes, milk and thyme that cooks all afternoon in the slow cooker, ladled over pasta with Parmesan. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 4–6 hours on high or 6–8 hours on low. Contains fish, milk and wheat. Per serving: about 690 kcal, 19g fat, 80g carbs, 49g protein.
instructions: Chop the onion, carrot, celery and 4 medium garlic cloves finely, or cut the vegetables into 1-inch chunks and pulse them in a food processor 15–20 times.

In the slow cooker, combine the vegetables, beef, pork, broth concentrate, milk, tomatoes, fish sauce, gelatin, mushroom seasoning, ¼ cup tomato paste, 2 teaspoons salt and 1 teaspoon pepper. Break the meat up small with a potato masher or wooden spoon.
Tuck the thyme sprigs into the meat (tie them with string if you want them easy to fish out). Cover and cook 4–6 hours on high or 6–8 hours on low.
Pull out the thyme, skim off extra fat, and season to taste.
Boil the pasta in salted water, stirring, until al dente, 8–9 minutes, and drain.
Divide the pasta into bowls, ladle the sauce over, and grate Parmesan on top.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken & Corn Tortilla Soup
description: Chicken, corn, jalapeño and chopped tortillas slow-cooked in enchilada sauce with chorizo chili spice until thick, with shredded chicken, crisp baked tortilla strips, cheese and lime on top. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 3–4 hours on high or 5–6 hours on low. Contains milk (cheese). Per serving: about 670 kcal, 28g fat, 62g carbs, 50g protein.
instructions: Chop the onion finely and set 1 cup aside for topping. Chop 6 large garlic cloves finely. Seed and finely chop the jalapeños. Chop 8 of the tortillas finely.

Season the chicken in the slow cooker with salt and pepper. Add the chopped vegetables, chorizo spice, chopped tortillas, corn, enchilada sauce, broth concentrate and 8 cups water. Cover and cook until the chicken is tender, 3–4 hours on high or 5–6 hours on low.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Stack the remaining tortillas, cut them in half, then cut across into ¼-inch strips. Toss them on a rimmed baking sheet with ¼ cup oil and some salt, and move half to a second sheet.
Bake the strips until crisp and lightly browned, 15–20 minutes, stirring and swapping the sheets halfway.
Lift the chicken onto a plate and shred it with 2 forks. Whisk the soup hard until the tortillas break down, stir the chicken back in, and season.
Chop the cilantro, leaves and stems, and cut the lime into wedges. Ladle the soup into bowls and top with cheese, tortilla strips, cilantro and lime.

title: Slow-Cooker Hoisin Garlic Chicken
description: Boneless chicken thighs braised until tender with hoisin, garlic and tomato paste, then shredded into a sticky, gently sweet and spicy glaze. Good on rice or noodles or in tortillas all week. Adapted from Sarah DiGregorio.
notes: About 2½ hours. It holds on warm for several hours. Don't skip reducing the sauce; that's what makes it glossy and sticky. A big batch keeps well: spoon it over rice or noodles, wrap it in tortillas, or shred it fine into buns with hot sauce like pulled pork.
instructions: Put the chicken, hoisin, chopped garlic, tomato paste, vinegar, garlic powder, crushed red pepper and 2 teaspoons salt in a 6- to 8-quart slow cooker. Cook on high for about 2 hours. It will hold on warm for several hours after that.
Lift the chicken onto a large rimmed platter or bowl with tongs.
Pour the sauce into a small saucepan and boil it hard over high heat until thick and syrupy, 10 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, pull the chicken into rough shreds with two forks. Pour the reduced sauce over and toss. Taste, adding salt, red pepper or vinegar if needed, and top with scallions if you like.

title: Smoky Spanish Pork Pan Roast
description: Pork tenderloin rubbed with smoked paprika, lemon and garlic, roasted on one pan over potatoes, peppers and onion, then drizzled with a lemon-cilantro chimichurri. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Cook the pork to 145°F. Per serving: about 710 kcal, 36g fat, 54g carbs, 43g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Halve the onion and cut it into ½-inch slices. Trim the peppers and halve them lengthwise. Scrub the potatoes and slice them into ¼-inch rounds.

Toss the potatoes, peppers and onion on a rimmed baking sheet with ¼ cup oil and a pinch each of salt and pepper, and spread them out (a little overlap is fine). Roast on the upper rack until the potatoes start to soften, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, grate 1 teaspoon each of garlic and lemon zest into a small bowl and squeeze in 2 tablespoons lemon juice, keeping the rest of the lemon. Whisk in 4 teaspoons smoked paprika, 2 teaspoons oil and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Pat the pork dry and rub the paste all over it. Set it on top of the vegetables, scraping any leftover paste onto the meat. Roast on the upper rack until the pork is almost done and slightly firm and the vegetables are tender, 15–20 minutes. Take the vegetables out before broiling if they are browning fast.
Meanwhile, roughly chop the cilantro, leaves and stems. Squeeze 1 tablespoon lemon juice into a medium bowl, whisk in the cilantro and ¼ cup oil, and season.

Turn the oven to broil and broil until the pork is lightly charred and reads 145°F inside and the vegetables are charred in spots, about 2 minutes. Watch closely. Rest the pork 3 minutes, slice it if you like, and serve with the vegetables and chimichurri.

title: Southern Macaroni and Cheese
description: A special-occasion baked mac and cheese: an egg and milk custard with extra-sharp Cheddar, a hidden layer of Colby Jack, and a broiled cheesy top. Adapted from NYT Cooking.
notes: About 45 minutes. The cheese is used in stages: 2 cups Cheddar in the macaroni and 2 cups on top; 1½ cups Colby Jack in the middle layer and ½ cup on top. Watch it under the broiler.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the macaroni until a little short of al dente, about 4 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water to stop the cooking.
Whisk the milk and eggs in a large bowl. Stir in the macaroni, 2 cups Cheddar, the melted butter, 1½ teaspoons salt and ½ teaspoon pepper until well mixed.
Spread half the macaroni in a 9x13-inch baking dish and sprinkle 1½ cups Colby Jack over it. Spread the rest of the macaroni on top. Cover with foil and bake on the middle rack for 30 minutes.
Take it out and remove the foil. Top with the remaining 2 cups Cheddar and ½ cup Colby Jack and broil on the top rack until browned in spots, 3 to 5 minutes. It can burn quickly, so stay close.
Let it cool until set, 10 to 15 minutes. It will look loose at first and firm up as it stands. Serve warm.

title: Soy-Glazed Beef Tenderloin
description: Tenderloin steaks seared and lacquered with sweet kecap manis, over rice cooked with red bell pepper, with a homemade peanut, sesame and gochugaru chili crisp spooned over. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Use less gochugaru for a milder chili crisp. Contains peanuts, sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 930 kcal, 50g fat, 81g carbs, 40g protein.
instructions: Seed and roughly chop the peppers. Bring them to a boil in a medium saucepan with the rice, 2 cups water and 1 teaspoon salt over high heat. Cover and cook on low until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, about 17 minutes. Keep covered.
Put the steaks in a large bowl, drizzle with half the kecap manis, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and turn to coat. Leave to marinate.

Grate 1 tablespoon garlic. Trim the scallions and slice them very thin, keeping the light and dark greens apart. Roughly chop the peanuts. Squeeze 2 tablespoons lime juice into a medium heatproof bowl and cut the rest of the lime into wedges.

Heat ½ cup oil in a large heavy skillet, cast iron if you have it, over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the light scallion greens, peanuts, garlic, all the sesame seeds, the gochugaru (less if you like) and 1 teaspoon sugar to the lime juice. Pour the hot oil over, stir, and set aside.

Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and cook the steaks until lightly charred and medium-rare, 3–4 minutes a side, or longer if you prefer. For the last 2–3 minutes, brush with the rest of the kecap manis, turning once or twice, until sticky and caramelized. Let them rest.
Season the chili crisp. Serve the steaks with the pepper rice, spoon the chili crisp over, and finish with the dark scallion greens and lime wedges.

title: Steak & Asparagus Stir-Fry
description: Thin-sliced steak tenderized in a cornstarch, tamari, mirin and baking soda marinade, seared hard with asparagus and garlic, and finished with a glossy sauce, peanuts and sesame oil. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. The marinade tenderizes the beef so it sears outside and stays soft inside; keep the heat high and move fast. Contains peanuts, sesame and soy. Per serving: about 720 kcal, 33g fat, 71g carbs, 34g protein.
instructions: Bring the rice and 2 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan over high heat. Cover and cook on low until tender and the water is absorbed, 17–20 minutes. Keep covered off the heat.

Pat the steak dry and slice it across the grain ¼ inch thick. Mix it in a large bowl with 1 packet of cornstarch, 2 teaspoons each of tamari, mirin and neutral oil, 1 teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon each of baking soda and sugar. Set aside.

Chop 2 large garlic cloves finely. Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut it into 2½-inch lengths. Microwave it, covered, until bright green and nearly crisp-tender, 1–2 minutes, then rinse under cold water and drain well. In another bowl, stir the broth concentrate with the rest of the cornstarch, mirin and tamari and ½ cup water.

Heat ¼ cup neutral oil in a large nonstick skillet over high heat until it smokes. Spread the beef in one layer and leave it until browned underneath, about 1 minute. Then stir and toss until nearly cooked with a little pink left, 30–60 seconds.
Push the beef to one side and cook the garlic in the space until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the asparagus and toss everything until the asparagus is crisp-tender, about 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce to loosen the cornstarch and pour it in. Toss until bubbling and lightly thickened, 30–45 seconds. Off the heat, stir in the peanuts and sesame oil. Serve over the rice.

title: Sweet & Spicy Shrimp Stir-Fry with Broccoli & Rice
description: A 15-minute stir-fry of shrimp and crisp-tender broccoli in sweet Thai chili sauce and tamari, over quick-heated rice. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Under 20 minutes. No microwave? Put the rice in a skillet, sprinkle with water, cover and steam over medium heat until hot, 2–3 minutes. Contains shellfish and soy. Per serving: about 470 kcal, 6g fat, 81g carbs, 30g protein.
instructions: Rinse the shrimp, pat dry, and season with salt and pepper.

Cut the broccoli into 1-inch florets if needed. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the broccoli, season, and cook, stirring now and then, until crisp-tender, 3–5 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook, stirring now and then, until pink and cooked through, about 3 minutes.
Add the Thai chili sauce, tamari and ¼ cup water and bring to a simmer. Take off the heat and season.
Heat the rice in the microwave following the package, or on the stove as in the notes, and serve the stir-fry over it.

title: Tangy Chicken, Tomato and Couscous Salad
description: Tagine flavors in a bowl: spiced couscous with chicken, prunes, sun-dried tomatoes and capers, crowned with juicy marinated cherry tomatoes. Adapted from Ashley Lonsdale.
notes: About 30 minutes. Simmering chopped rotisserie chicken in the salted water turns it into a quick stock that flavors the couscous as it plumps.
instructions: Toss the cherry tomatoes in a medium bowl with salt, pepper, the parsley and 2 tablespoons of oil from the sun-dried tomato jar. Set aside.

Heat the other 2 tablespoons of sun-dried tomato oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the chicken, sun-dried tomatoes, prunes, cumin and ginger and stir until sizzling and fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the water, bring to a boil over high heat, and salt it to taste. Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and leave 5 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon juice, capers and caper brine. Spoon onto a platter while warm and pile the tomatoes on top.

title: Tex-Mex Turkey Frito Pie
description: A one-skillet Frito pie: ground turkey chili with peppers, onion, salsa and chorizo chili spice, topped with corn chips and cheese and broiled. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains milk. Per serving: about 710 kcal, 47g fat, 39g carbs, 36g protein.
instructions: Halve and roughly chop the onion. Seed the bell peppers and cut them into ½-inch pieces. Set aside 1 tablespoon each of onion and pepper for topping. Pick the cilantro leaves and keep them in a damp paper towel; chop the stems finely.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large cast-iron skillet. Add the turkey, season, and cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 5 minutes.

Set a rack in the upper third of the oven and turn on the broiler. Add the rest of the onion and peppers to the turkey and cook, stirring now and then, until tender and starting to brown, 5–7 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro stems and 1 packet chorizo chili spice (more or less to taste) until fragrant. Add all the salsa and 1 cup water, bring to a simmer, take off the heat, and season.
Cover the chili with an even layer of Fritos, then the cheese. Broil until melted, 1–3 minutes, watching carefully.
Top with the cilantro leaves and the saved peppers and onion.

title: Thai Lemongrass Steak with Coconut Rice & Cucumber Salad
description: Seared steaks in a lemongrass, curry paste and coconut pan sauce, with lime-scented coconut rice, a cucumber ribbon salad in a fish sauce and lime dressing, and chopped peanuts. Makes a generous batch. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains fish, peanuts, sesame, soy, tree nuts and wheat. Per serving: about 710 kcal, 35g fat, 74g carbs, 28g protein.
instructions: Bring the rice, 2 cups each of water and coconut milk, and 2 teaspoons each of sugar and salt to a boil in a large saucepan. Cover and cook on low until tender and the liquid is absorbed, 17–20 minutes. Keep covered.

Zest the lime and squeeze 2 tablespoons juice, keeping them apart, and cut the rest into wedges. Pick the cilantro leaves and keep them in a damp paper towel; chop the stems finely. Grate 1 teaspoon garlic. Slice the jalapeños thin. Halve the red onion and thinly slice ½ cup, saving the rest. Roughly chop the peanuts.

In a large bowl, mix the cilantro stems, garlic, lime juice, 1 teaspoon of the zest, ¼ cup oil, 1½ tablespoons fish sauce and 3 teaspoons sugar. Season, then toss in the onion and jalapeños. Shave the cucumber into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and add them to the bowl, but don't toss until just before serving.

Pat the steaks dry and season them. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the steaks in batches until browned and medium-rare, 2–4 minutes a side, adding oil between batches if needed. Let them rest on a plate.

Lower the heat to medium, add ¼ cup water, and simmer while scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the lemongrass spice, 2 teaspoons curry paste and the rest of the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Add 1 tablespoon sugar and 2 teaspoons vinegar and season.

Fluff the rice, stir in the remaining lime zest, and plate it. Toss the cucumbers in their dressing and add them alongside with the peanuts on top. Slice the steaks thin, lay them over the rice, spoon the sauce over, and finish with cilantro leaves and lime.

title: Chicken al Limone
description: Garlic and lemon-marinated chicken tossed with spaghetti in a buttery lemon pan sauce, with sautéed garlic spinach, parsley and Parmesan. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 20–30 minutes. Contains milk and wheat. Per serving: about 760 kcal, 32g fat, 68g carbs, 50g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti, stirring so it doesn't stick, until al dente, 8–10 minutes. Save 2 cups of the water and drain.

Chop 2 tablespoons garlic finely. Grate the lemon zest into a medium bowl and squeeze the juice of 2 lemons into a small bowl. Pat the chicken dry and toss it with the zest, 2 tablespoons of the juice, half the garlic, 2 tablespoons oil, 1 teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper. Leave it to marinate.
Pick and finely chop the parsley leaves.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir the rest of the garlic for about 30 seconds. Add the spinach, season, and cook until just wilted, about 2 minutes. Move to a plate, cover, and wipe out the skillet.

Whisk the broth concentrate with the rest of the lemon juice and 1½ cups of the pasta water. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat, add the chicken in one layer, and leave it until browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Stir and cook until done, about 2 minutes more. Move to a bowl.

Add the broth mixture and 4 tablespoons butter to the skillet and stir until melted. Add the spaghetti, the chicken and its juices, and more pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce is how you like it. Top with parsley and half the Parmesan, and serve the spinach and the rest of the Parmesan alongside.

title: Vietnamese Caramel Pork Bánh Mì
description: Crusty baguettes spread with mayo and filled with caramel-glazed pulled pork, quick-pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: 30–40 minutes. Contains egg, fish, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 1020 kcal, 57g fat, 106g carbs, 21g protein.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Peel the carrot and daikon and cut them into thin matchsticks, or grate them on the large holes of a box grater. Pack them into a shallow bowl.
Bring ¼ cup each of vinegar and water, 3 tablespoons sugar and ½ teaspoon salt to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat.
Pour the hot brine over the carrot and daikon and leave them to pickle until serving.

Peel the cucumber if you like, halve it lengthwise, scoop out the seeds, and cut it into 4- to 5-inch sticks. Seed the jalapeño if you like and slice as much as you want. Cut the cilantro, leaves and stems, into 2-inch lengths. Chop 2 tablespoons garlic finely.
Pat the pork dry and break it into bite-size pieces.
Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it just smokes. Cook the pork, stirring now and then, until browned and crusty in places, 2–4 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add 1 tablespoon oil and ¼ cup sugar to the skillet and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until the sugar turns deep amber, 3–5 minutes.
Add the pork and garlic and stir until coated in caramel and fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the fish sauce, 2 teaspoons vinegar and ½ cup water.
Cook over medium-high heat until the liquid has nearly gone and the pork is sticky, 2–4 minutes.
Split the baguettes lengthwise, leaving one side attached, and pull out some of the soft inside. Close them and bake on the middle rack until the crust is golden, about 5 minutes.
Spread mayonnaise inside the rolls, add the pork, and fill with the pickles, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño. Cut in half if you like.

title: Vietnamese Chicken & Shrimp Noodle Salad
description: Rice noodles with shredded cabbage, onion, bell pepper, mint and cilantro, topped with seared chicken and shrimp in a sweet lime and fish sauce dressing, peanuts and sriracha. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Contains fish, peanuts and shellfish. Per serving: about 690 kcal, 31g fat, 86g carbs, 56g protein.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Chop 1 tablespoon garlic finely. Zest 1 lime and squeeze ¼ cup juice into a large bowl. Cut any remaining lime into wedges.
Whisk the fish sauce, garlic and ¼ cup sugar into the lime juice and zest until the sugar dissolves.

Pat the shrimp and chicken dry and season them. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until browned on one side, about 3 minutes. Turn it, add the shrimp, and cook, turning as needed, until both are done, 3–4 minutes more. Toss them in the dressing.
Cook all the rice noodles, stirring now and then so they don't stick, until tender, 8–9 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with 1 teaspoon oil.

Halve the cabbage and slice it into thin ribbons. Halve and thinly slice the onion. Seed the bell peppers and slice them into thin strips. Pick the mint and cilantro leaves, chop them roughly, and toss them with the chicken and shrimp.
Crush or chop the peanuts. Arrange the vegetables and noodles on a platter, top with the chicken, shrimp and dressing, and finish with peanuts and sriracha.

title: Yaki Udon with Bacon & Cabbage
description: A 15-minute stir-fry of chewy udon, bacon and shredded cabbage in a mirin, tamari and hondashi sauce, finished with furikake. Adapted from Marley Spoon.
notes: Under 20 minutes; serves 4. Contains fish, sesame, soy and wheat. Per serving: about 550 kcal, 23g fat, 51g carbs, 30g protein.
instructions: Cut the bacon into 1-inch strips. Stir the mirin, tamari and 2 teaspoons hondashi together in a small bowl until dissolved.
Put the bacon and 2 teaspoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring now and then, until the fat has run out and the bacon is browned but not crisp, 3–4 minutes.
Add the cabbage blend and stir for 1 minute. Add the noodles and the tamari mixture, cover, and cook until everything softens, about 2 minutes.
Uncover and toss to loosen the noodles and mix everything through. Season if needed and sprinkle with furikake to serve.

title: Zuni Chicken with Bread Salad
description: A whole chicken dry-brined with thyme and garlic under the skin and roasted very hot in cast iron, with a warm bread salad of toasted bread, currants, pine nuts, scallions and a sharp vinaigrette. Adapted from Food & Wine.
notes: Start a day or two ahead: the chicken needs at least 24 and up to 48 hours uncovered in the fridge. The oven starts at 450°F for the bread salad and goes up to 500°F for the chicken. Keep a quarter of the dressing back to finish the salad. Our saved copy was missing the original's last step on finishing the salad with greens.
instructions: Work your fingers under the skin of the breasts and thighs to loosen it. Spread the thyme and garlic evenly under the skin, then season the bird all over with salt and pepper. Set it on a rack over a rimmed baking sheet and refrigerate, uncovered, for 24 to 48 hours.
For the bread salad, heat the oven to 450°F. Soak the currants in 1 tablespoon warm water and the red wine vinegar in a small bowl until plump, about 10 minutes, then drain.
Whisk ½ cup olive oil with the Champagne vinegar and season to make the dressing.

Toss the bread with 2 tablespoons olive oil on a rimmed baking sheet and bake, turning once, until lightly toasted, 8 to 12 minutes. When cool enough to handle, 5 to 10 minutes, tear it into bite-size pieces of 1 to 1½ inches. Toss with three quarters of the dressing (about ½ cup) in a large bowl and let it soak in, about 15 minutes.

Heat ½ tablespoon olive oil in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium-low heat and cook the scallions and garlic, stirring often, until soft, about 2 minutes. Stir in the pine nuts and add it all to the bread with the currants. Toss well.

Spoon the bread salad into a shallow 8-inch square baking dish. Cover loosely with foil and bake until hot, about 15 minutes. Uncover and bake until the tops are dry and the bottoms lightly browned, 6 to 10 minutes. Set aside.

Raise the oven to 500°F. Wipe out the skillet and heat it in the oven for 8 minutes. Take it out, swirl in the remaining 1½ tablespoons oil, pat the chicken dry, and set it in breast side up. Roast until the thigh juices run clear and a thermometer in the thickest part of the breast and thigh reads at least 160°F to 165°F, 45 to 55 minutes. Rest on a board, uncovered, for 10 minutes.
Carve the chicken and serve it with the bread salad, tossed with the reserved dressing.
